questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: What are the cells of cartilage called?
questions.why: Chondrocytes are the cells of cartilage. Each one sits in its own small cavity in the matrix called a lacuna, and together they maintain the firm, gel-like cartilage matrix around them. The prefix chondro- means cartilage, which is a quick way to separate them from the bone cells, whose names start with osteo-.
notes: Correct. Chondrocytes are the cartilage cells, each housed in a lacuna.
Osteoblasts are the bone-building cells that secrete new bone matrix. Choose them if the question asked which cell lays down new bone.
Fibroblasts are the cells of connective tissue proper that make fibers such as collagen. They would fit a question about the main cell of dense or areolar connective tissue, not cartilage.
Osteocytes are mature bone cells sitting in lacunae within hard bone matrix. They would be the answer if the question asked which cell maintains bone matrix day to day.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: What is the connective tissue sheath wrapped around most cartilage called?
questions.why: The perichondrium is a sheath of dense connective tissue that wraps most cartilage. The name breaks down as peri- (around) plus chondr- (cartilage). It is also the source of new cartilage during appositional growth, when cartilage is added at its outer surface.
notes: Correct. The perichondrium is the sheath around most cartilage.
The endosteum is the thin membrane lining the internal surfaces of bone, such as the medullary cavity. Pick it if the question asked what lines the inside of a bone.
The epimysium is the connective tissue layer wrapping an entire skeletal muscle. It would be right for a question about muscle coverings, which follow the same peri- and epi- naming pattern.
The periosteum is the connective tissue membrane covering the outer surface of a bone. It would be the answer if the question were about the covering of a bone rather than of cartilage.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which type of cartilage is the most common in the body?
questions.why: Hyaline cartilage is the most common type. It has fine collagen fibers that give it a glassy, smooth look, and it is found at the ends of long bones, in the nose, in the airways, and in the costal cartilages that join the ribs to the sternum. It also forms the model that most bones replace as they develop.
notes: Elastic cartilage has many elastic fibers, which make it flexible and springy. It would be the answer for a question about the cartilage of the external ear or the epiglottis.
Fibrocartilage has thick bundles of collagen, making it tough and shock-absorbing. Choose it for a question about the intervertebral discs, the knee menisci, or the pubic symphysis.
Correct. Hyaline cartilage is the most common cartilage in the body.

Calcified cartilage is not one of the three cartilage types. It describes cartilage whose matrix has hardened, as in the zone of calcification of the growth plate, so it fits a growth plate question instead.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which bone shape class describes the carpals and tarsals?
questions.why: Short bones are roughly cube-shaped, about as long as they are wide. The carpals of the wrist and the tarsals of the ankle are the classic examples. Their blocky shape suits joints that need many small gliding movements rather than long levers.
notes: Long bones are longer than they are wide, with a shaft and two ends, like the femur and humerus. They would be the answer if the question named the bones of the arm, thigh, or the metacarpals and phalanges.
Correct. The carpals and tarsals are short, roughly cube-shaped bones.
Flat bones are thin and often curved, like the sternum, the ribs, and most skull bones. Pick this class for a question about bones that protect organs as broad plates.
Irregular bones have complex shapes that fit no other group, like the vertebrae and hip bones. They would fit a question about a vertebra, not a wrist or ankle bone.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: What is the shaft of a long bone called?
questions.why: The diaphysis is the shaft of a long bone, a tube of compact bone wrapped around a hollow medullary cavity. It forms most of the bone's length and carries weight along the long axis. The expanded ends on either side are the epiphyses.
notes: The medullary cavity is the hollow space inside the diaphysis that holds marrow. It is inside the shaft rather than the shaft itself, so pick it for a question about where yellow marrow is stored.
The epiphysis is each expanded end of a long bone, made of spongy bone under a thin compact shell. It would be the answer if the question asked about the ends of the bone.
Correct. The diaphysis is the shaft of a long bone.
The metaphysis is the region between the shaft and an end, where the growth plate or its remnant sits. Choose it for a question about where the diaphysis and epiphysis meet.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: What is the structural unit of compact bone called?
questions.why: The osteon, also called the Haversian system, is the structural unit of compact bone. Each osteon is a cylinder of concentric rings of matrix (lamellae) around a central canal that carries blood vessels and nerves. Osteons run along the length of the bone, which makes compact bone strong along its long axis.
notes: Correct. The osteon is the structural unit of compact bone.
A canaliculus is a tiny channel linking lacunae so osteocytes can exchange materials. Pick it for a question about how osteocytes communicate and receive nutrients.
A trabecula is a single strut in the open lattice of spongy bone. It would be the answer if the question asked for the structural unit of spongy bone instead of compact bone.
A lamella is one ring of matrix within an osteon. It is a part of the osteon rather than the whole unit, so choose it if the question asked about the rings around the central canal.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which bone cell builds and secretes new bone matrix?
questions.why: The osteoblast is the bone-building cell that secretes new bone matrix. Once an osteoblast becomes surrounded by the matrix it has made, it settles into a lacuna and becomes an osteocyte. A simple memory aid is that osteoblasts build bone.
notes: The osteocyte is a mature bone cell in a lacuna that maintains the matrix day to day. Choose it if the question asked about the cell that keeps existing bone healthy rather than building new bone.
Correct. Osteoblasts build and secrete new bone matrix.
The osteoclast is the large, multinucleated cell that breaks down and resorbs bone matrix. It would be the answer if the question asked which cell removes bone.
The osteogenic cell is the stem cell of bone tissue that divides to produce new osteoblasts. Pick it for a question about which cell gives rise to the bone builders.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which bone cell breaks down and resorbs bone matrix?
questions.why: The osteoclast breaks down and resorbs bone matrix. It is a large cell with many nuclei, and unlike the other three bone cells, it comes from a blood-cell line. Its work is balanced by osteoblasts, which build new matrix, so bone is constantly being reshaped.
notes: The osteoblast builds and secretes new bone matrix, which is the opposite job. It would be the answer if the question asked which cell lays down bone.
Correct. Osteoclasts break down and resorb bone.
The osteocyte is a mature bone cell that maintains the matrix from inside a lacuna. Pick it for a question about the most common cell in mature bone.
The osteogenic cell is the bone stem cell that divides to make osteoblasts. Choose it if the question asked about the cell that starts the bone-building lineage.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which type of cartilage is found in the external ear and the epiglottis?
questions.why: Elastic cartilage contains many elastic fibers in its matrix, which makes it flexible and springy. That is why the external ear bends and springs back, and why the epiglottis can flip down over the larynx and return to position. Both structures need to bend repeatedly without losing their shape.
notes: Correct. Elastic cartilage forms the external ear and the epiglottis.
Hyaline cartilage has fine collagen fibers and a glassy look. It would be the answer for the nose, the airways, the costal cartilages, or the ends of long bones.
Fibrocartilage has thick collagen bundles and resists compression. Choose it for the intervertebral discs, the knee menisci, or the pubic symphysis.
Articular cartilage is the hyaline cartilage that caps the ends of bones at a joint. It is a location name rather than a separate type, so pick it only for a question about joint surfaces.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: What is the hollow core of the diaphysis that holds marrow called?
questions.why: The medullary cavity is the hollow space running down the middle of the diaphysis. In an adult it stores yellow marrow, which is mostly fat. Making the shaft a hollow tube keeps the bone strong while saving weight.
notes: The metaphysis is the region between the diaphysis and an epiphysis, holding the growth plate or its remnant. Pick it if the question asked where the shaft widens into the end.
Correct. The medullary cavity is the marrow-filled core of the diaphysis.
A lacuna is a tiny cavity in the matrix that houses one osteocyte or chondrocyte. Choose it for a question about where a single bone or cartilage cell sits.

The central canal is the small channel at the core of a single osteon, carrying blood vessels and nerves. It would be the answer if the question were about the microscopic canal inside an osteon, not the large cavity of the whole shaft.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: What is the open lattice of bony struts that forms spongy bone called?
questions.why: Trabeculae are the thin bony struts that form the open lattice of spongy bone. They line up along the lines of stress the bone experiences, so spongy bone stays strong while being much lighter than compact bone. The spaces between trabeculae hold red marrow.
notes: Lamellae are the concentric rings of matrix in compact bone. They would be the answer for a question about the rings around a central canal.
Correct. Trabeculae are the bony struts of spongy bone.
Osteons are the cylindrical structural units of compact bone. Pick them if the question asked what compact bone is built from, since spongy bone has no osteons.
Canaliculi are tiny channels that connect lacunae so osteocytes can exchange materials. Choose them for a question about how osteocytes receive nutrients.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Cartilage has no blood vessels of its own. What is the direct result of this?
questions.why: Cartilage is avascular, meaning it has no blood vessels of its own. Nutrients must diffuse slowly through the matrix to reach the chondrocytes, and repair cells and supplies cannot be delivered quickly. As a result, damaged cartilage, such as a torn meniscus, heals slowly and often incompletely.
notes: Cartilage is actually firm but flexible, and elastic cartilage is especially springy. This choice confuses lacking blood vessels with lacking flexibility, which are unrelated properties.
Correct. Without blood vessels, cartilage repairs itself slowly.
Cartilage does contain living cells, the chondrocytes, sitting in lacunae. This choice mixes up having no blood vessels with having no cells.
All three cartilage types contain collagen, from the fine fibers of hyaline cartilage to the thick bundles of fibrocartilage. This choice reflects a misconception that avascular means fiber-free.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which type of cartilage forms the intervertebral discs and the knee menisci?
questions.why: Fibrocartilage contains thick bundles of collagen fibers, which make it tough and good at absorbing shock. That suits the intervertebral discs and the knee menisci, which take heavy compressive loads with every step. The pubic symphysis is another fibrocartilage joint.
notes: Articular cartilage is the hyaline cartilage covering bone ends inside a joint. Pick it for a question about the smooth surface where two bones glide, not for discs or menisci.
Correct. Fibrocartilage forms the discs and the menisci.
Hyaline cartilage is the smooth, glassy, most common type. It would be the answer for the ends of long bones, the airways, the nose, or the costal cartilages.
Elastic cartilage is springy because of its many elastic fibers. Choose it for the external ear or the epiglottis.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: A small bone forms within a tendon, as the patella does. Which shape class does it belong to?
questions.why: Sesamoid bones are small bones that develop inside a tendon. The patella, or kneecap, is the classic example, sitting in the tendon of the quadriceps muscle as it crosses the knee. The name comes from their resemblance to sesame seeds.
notes: Short bones are roughly cube-shaped, like the carpals and tarsals. Choose this class for wrist and ankle bones.
Correct. A bone that forms within a tendon is a sesamoid bone.
Flat bones are thin, often curved plates such as the sternum, ribs, and most skull bones. Pick this class for a broad protective bone.
Irregular bones have complex shapes that fit no other group, like vertebrae and hip bones. They would be the answer for a bone defined by its odd shape rather than by forming in a tendon.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which membrane covers the outer surface of a bone, and which lines its internal surfaces?
questions.why: The periosteum is the connective tissue membrane on the outer surface of a bone, and perforating (Sharpey) fibers anchor it firmly into the bone beneath. The endosteum is a thin membrane lining the internal surfaces, including the medullary cavity. The prefixes help: peri- means around, and endo- means within.
notes: Correct. The periosteum is outside and the endosteum lines the inside.
This reverses the two membranes. Students choose it when they mix up the prefixes, but endo- means within, so the endosteum is always the inner lining.
The perichondrium is never inside a bone, since it is the sheath around cartilage. Choose it for a cartilage question, and keep the endosteum as the inner lining of bone.
The perichondrium wraps cartilage, not bone. It would be correct only if the question asked about the sheath around a piece of cartilage.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which structure caps the epiphysis where one bone meets another at a joint?
questions.why: Articular cartilage is a layer of hyaline cartilage that caps the epiphysis where it meets another bone. Its smooth, slick surface reduces friction and cushions the bone ends as the joint moves. Because it has no blood supply, damage to it heals poorly.
notes: The epiphyseal line is the bony remnant of the growth plate, found deep inside the bone at the metaphysis. Pick it for a question about what remains after growth in length ends.
The endosteum lines the internal surfaces of bone, such as the medullary cavity. Choose it if the question asked what lines the inside of a bone.
Correct. Articular cartilage caps the epiphysis at the joint.
The periosteum covers the outer bone surface everywhere except at the joint surfaces. It would be the answer for a question about the membrane covering the shaft.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which canal of compact bone runs crosswise and links the central canals of neighboring osteons?
questions.why: Perforating canals, also called Volkmann canals, run crosswise through compact bone, roughly at right angles to the osteons. They connect the central canals of neighboring osteons with each other and with the periosteum and medullary cavity, so blood vessels and nerves can reach every osteon.
notes: A canaliculus is a hair-thin channel connecting lacunae within an osteon. Choose it for a question about how individual osteocytes exchange materials.
The central canal runs lengthwise down the core of each osteon. It would be the answer if the question asked about the canal in the middle of one osteon.
Correct. Perforating canals run crosswise and link the central canals.
The medullary cavity is the large hollow core of the diaphysis that holds marrow. Pick it for a question about where marrow is stored in the shaft.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which tiny channels connect the lacunae and let osteocytes exchange materials?
questions.why: Canaliculi are tiny channels running through the hard matrix between lacunae. They link osteocytes to each other and to the central canal, so nutrients and wastes can pass from cell to cell. Without them, osteocytes buried in mineralized matrix could not survive.
notes: Lamellae are the rings of matrix around the central canal. They are the solid layers that canaliculi pass through, so choose them for a question about the concentric rings of an osteon.
Central canals are the larger channels at the core of each osteon, carrying blood vessels and nerves. They would be the answer if the question asked where the blood supply of an osteon runs.
Trabeculae are the bony struts of spongy bone. Pick them for a question about the lattice that fills the epiphyses.
Correct. Canaliculi connect lacunae so osteocytes can exchange materials.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which bone cell comes from a blood-cell line, unlike the other three bone cells?
questions.why: Three of the four bone cells form one lineage: the osteogenic cell divides to make osteoblasts, and osteoblasts become osteocytes. The osteoclast is the outsider. It comes from a blood-cell line, is large with many nuclei, and is the only bone cell that takes bone away.
notes: Correct. The osteoclast arises from a blood-cell line.
The osteocyte is a mature osteoblast that has become trapped in matrix, so it is part of the bone lineage. Choose it for a question about the cell maintaining matrix inside a lacuna.
The osteoblast comes from the osteogenic cell, so it belongs to the bone lineage. It would be the answer if the question asked which cell secretes new matrix.
The osteogenic cell is the stem cell at the start of the bone lineage. Pick it if the question asked which cell divides to produce osteoblasts.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which route of ossification builds the flat bones of the skull?
questions.why: In intramembranous ossification, bone forms directly within a sheet of connective tissue membrane, with no cartilage model first. This is how the flat bones of the skull form. The name tells the story: intra- (within) a membrane.
notes: Appositional growth is how a bone grows wider by adding bone beneath the periosteum. It describes growth of an existing bone, so choose it for a question about a bone thickening.
Endochondral ossification builds bone by replacing a hyaline cartilage model. It would be the answer for most bones of the body, such as the long bones of the limbs.
Interstitial growth is growth from within, as at the epiphyseal plate when a long bone lengthens. Pick it for a question about how a long bone grows longer.
Correct. The flat skull bones form by intramembranous ossification.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which route of ossification forms most bones of the body by replacing a cartilage model?
questions.why: Endochondral ossification forms most bones of the body. A model of hyaline cartilage is laid down first, and bone gradually replaces it. The name means within (endo-) cartilage (chondr-), which describes where the bone forms.
notes: Intramembranous ossification forms bone directly within a connective tissue membrane, with no cartilage model. It would be the answer for the flat bones of the skull.
Correct. Endochondral ossification replaces a cartilage model and forms most bones.
Interstitial growth is growth from within, which lengthens a long bone at the epiphyseal plate. Pick it for a question about growth in length.
Appositional growth adds bone at the outer surface so a bone grows wider. Choose it for a question about thickening, not about how a bone first forms.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: At which structure does a long bone grow longer?
questions.why: The epiphyseal plate, or growth plate, is a disc of hyaline cartilage in the metaphysis between the shaft and the end. Cartilage there keeps growing and is replaced by bone on the shaft side, which pushes the epiphysis farther away and lengthens the bone. When growth ends, the plate closes and leaves the epiphyseal line.
notes: Articular cartilage caps the bone end at the joint and does not drive lengthening. Pick it for a question about the smooth joint surface.
The periosteum is where a bone grows wider, through appositional growth. It would be the answer if the question asked where a bone increases in width.
Correct. Long bones lengthen at the epiphyseal plate.
The medullary cavity is the hollow marrow space in the shaft. It enlarges as the bone grows, but it is not where lengthening happens. Choose it for a question about where yellow marrow is stored.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Appositional growth changes a long bone in which way?
questions.why: Appositional growth adds new bone at the outer surface, beneath the periosteum, so the bone grows wider. Apposition means placing something next to something else, which describes laying new layers on the surface. At the same time, bone is removed from the inner surface so the medullary cavity widens too.
notes: Appositional growth does not remove marrow. This choice confuses adding bone on the outside with the inner remodeling that actually enlarges the marrow cavity.
Correct. Appositional growth makes a bone wider.
Growth in length happens through interstitial growth at the epiphyseal plate. This would be the answer if the question asked about interstitial growth.
No normal growth process makes a bone shorter. This choice reflects a mix-up between growth and bone loss.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which type of cartilage growth adds new cartilage at the outer surface, from the perichondrium?
questions.why: Cartilage grows in two directions. In appositional growth, cells from the perichondrium add new cartilage at the outer surface. In interstitial growth, chondrocytes divide inside the matrix and the cartilage expands from within.
notes: Interstitial growth expands cartilage from within, as chondrocytes divide inside the matrix. It would be the answer if the question described growth from the inside.
Endochondral ossification is the process of bone replacing a cartilage model. Choose it for a question about how most bones form, not how cartilage grows.
Correct. Appositional growth adds cartilage at the surface from the perichondrium.
Intramembranous ossification forms bone directly within a membrane. Pick it for a question about the flat bones of the skull.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: What is the remnant of the growth plate after growth in length ends called?
questions.why: When a long bone stops growing in length, the cartilage of the growth plate is fully replaced by bone. What is left is a thin bony line, the epiphyseal line, in the metaphysis. Seeing it on an X-ray tells a clinician the skeleton is mature.
notes: Articular cartilage is the hyaline cartilage on the joint surface of the epiphysis. Choose it for a question about what covers the bone end at a joint.
Correct. The epiphyseal line is the remnant of the closed growth plate.
The epiphyseal plate is the active cartilage growth plate of a still-growing bone. It would be the answer if the question asked where a child's bone lengthens.
The diaphysis is the shaft of the long bone. Pick it for a question about the long middle portion of the bone.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which structural difference distinguishes spongy bone from compact bone?
options: Spongy bone has no bone cells
questions.why: Compact bone is built from osteons, each with a central canal. Spongy bone has no osteons; instead it is an open lattice of trabeculae with red marrow in the spaces. On a slide, the quickest way to tell them apart is to look for central canals.
notes: This reverses the real difference. Osteons are the units of compact bone, so a tissue full of them would be compact bone, not spongy bone.
Spongy bone does contain bone cells, including osteocytes in lacunae within the trabeculae. Students pick this when they confuse lacking osteons with lacking cells.
Correct. Spongy bone is built from trabeculae and has no osteons.
Spongy bone has true bone matrix in every trabecula. This choice mistakes the open spaces between struts for an absence of matrix.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which structure houses a single osteocyte within compact bone?
questions.why: A lacuna is a small cavity in the matrix, and in bone each one holds a single osteocyte. Lacunae sit between the lamellae of an osteon and are linked to each other by canaliculi. Cartilage uses the same arrangement, with a chondrocyte in each lacuna.
notes: A lamella is one ring of bony matrix around the central canal. Choose it for a question about the concentric layers of an osteon.
Correct. Each osteocyte sits in its own lacuna.
A canaliculus is a hair-thin channel running between lacunae. It would be the answer for a question about how osteocytes exchange materials.
The central canal is the channel at the core of an osteon carrying blood vessels and nerves. Pick it if the question asked what runs down the center of the osteon.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: A bone is described as longer than it is wide, with a shaft and two ends. Which shape class and example fit this description?
options: An irregular bone, such as a vertebra
A short bone, such as a carpal
A flat bone, such as the sternum
A long bone, such as the humerus
questions.why: Long bones are defined by being longer than they are wide, with a shaft (the diaphysis) and two expanded ends (the epiphyses). The humerus fits that description exactly. Size does not decide the class, since even the small phalanges of the fingers are long bones.
notes: A vertebra is an irregular bone with a complex shape. This pairing fits a question about bones that fit no other shape group.
A carpal is a short bone, roughly cube-shaped. This pairing fits a question about blocky wrist or ankle bones.
The sternum is a flat bone, thin and plate-like, with no shaft. This pairing would be right for a question about a broad, thin protective bone.
Correct. The humerus is a long bone with a shaft and two ends.
questions.answerText: A long bone, such as the humerus

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: A compact bone slide shows concentric rings of matrix surrounding a single canal that carries blood vessels. What is the canal at the core?
questions.why: The rings are lamellae, and together with the canal they form an osteon. The canal at the core of each osteon is the central canal, also called the Haversian canal, and it carries blood vessels and nerves along the length of the bone. Finding central canals on a slide is how you confirm you are looking at compact bone.
notes: A perforating canal runs crosswise between osteons rather than sitting at the center of the rings. It would be the answer for a canal that links neighboring central canals.
The medullary cavity is the large marrow space of the whole shaft, not a canal inside one osteon. Pick it for a question about where yellow marrow is stored.
Correct. The central canal sits at the core of the osteon.
A canaliculus is a hair-thin channel between lacunae, far too small to carry blood vessels. Choose it for a question about how osteocytes connect to one another.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: A child's X-ray of a long bone shows a dark band of cartilage between the shaft and the expanded end. Which structure is this band?
questions.why: The epiphyseal plate is a disc of hyaline cartilage in the metaphysis, between the diaphysis and the epiphysis. Cartilage is not mineralized, so on an X-ray it looks like a gap or dark band in the bone. Its presence means the bone is still growing in length.
notes: Correct. The cartilage band in a child's bone is the epiphyseal plate.
The medullary cavity is the marrow space inside the shaft, running lengthwise, not a band across the bone near its end. Choose it for a question about where marrow is stored.
Articular cartilage sits on the outer joint surface of the epiphysis, not between the shaft and the end. Pick it for a question about the surface where two bones meet.
The epiphyseal line is the bony remnant left after the plate closes, so it shows up in adults, not as a cartilage band in a child. It would be the answer for an adult X-ray.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: A section through the epiphysis of a long bone shows an open lattice of bony struts with marrow in the spaces and no osteons. Which tissue is this?
questions.why: The epiphyses of long bones are filled with spongy bone under a thin shell of compact bone. Spongy bone is an open lattice of trabeculae, the bony struts, with red marrow filling the spaces between them. It has no osteons, and that missing central canal is the clue that separates it from compact bone.
notes: Correct. A lattice of trabeculae with marrow and no osteons is spongy bone.
Hyaline cartilage is a smooth, glassy tissue with chondrocytes in lacunae and no bony struts. Choose it for a section of articular cartilage or the growth plate.
Fibrocartilage has thick parallel bundles of collagen and no marrow spaces. Pick it for a section of an intervertebral disc or a knee meniscus.
Compact bone is dense and built from osteons with central canals. It would be the answer if the section showed tightly packed rings around canals, as in the wall of the shaft.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: A long bone is increasing in width, with new bone being added at its outer surface beneath the periosteum. Which type of growth is this?
questions.why: Appositional growth adds new bone in layers at the outer surface, beneath the periosteum, so the bone gets wider. It continues throughout life, which is why bones can thicken in response to use. Growth in length is a separate process that happens at the epiphyseal plate.
notes: Interstitial growth is growth from within, which lengthens a long bone at the epiphyseal plate. It would be the answer if the bone were getting longer rather than wider.
Correct. Adding bone beneath the periosteum to widen the bone is appositional growth.
Endochondral ossification is how most bones first form by replacing a cartilage model. Pick it for a question about how a long bone develops before birth.
Intramembranous ossification is how flat skull bones first form within a membrane. Choose it for a question about the origin of the skull bones, not the widening of a long bone.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: A flat bone of the skull is forming directly within a sheet of connective tissue membrane, with no cartilage model. Which route of ossification is this?
questions.why: Intramembranous ossification forms bone directly inside a connective tissue membrane, skipping the cartilage stage. The flat bones of the skull form this way. The absence of a cartilage model is the clue that rules out endochondral ossification.
notes: Correct. Bone forming directly within a membrane is intramembranous ossification.
Interstitial growth is growth from within an existing tissue, such as a long bone lengthening at its growth plate. Choose it for a question about growth in length.
Endochondral ossification needs a hyaline cartilage model that bone then replaces. It would be the answer for a long bone of the limb forming from cartilage.
Appositional growth adds layers at the surface to make a bone wider. Pick it for a question about a bone thickening beneath the periosteum.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which list gives the five zones of the growth plate in order, from the epiphysis toward the diaphysis?
options: Proliferation, resting cartilage, hypertrophy, calcification, ossification
Ossification, calcification, hypertrophy, proliferation, resting cartilage
Resting cartilage, hypertrophy, proliferation, ossification, calcification
Resting cartilage, proliferation, hypertrophy, calcification, ossification
questions.why: The growth plate reads like a timeline from the epiphysis down. Resting cartilage anchors the plate to the epiphysis, cells in the zone of proliferation divide and stack into columns, cells in the zone of hypertrophy enlarge, the matrix hardens in the zone of calcification, and bone replaces the cartilage in the zone of ossification next to the diaphysis.
notes: This puts proliferation ahead of resting cartilage. The resting zone must come first because it is the layer that anchors the plate to the epiphysis.
This is the correct sequence read backward, from the diaphysis toward the epiphysis. It would be right only if the question asked for the order starting at the shaft.

This swaps two pairs. Cells must divide before they can enlarge, and the matrix must calcify before bone can replace it, so the true order is proliferation then hypertrophy, and calcification then ossification.
Correct. Resting, proliferation, hypertrophy, calcification, ossification is the order.
questions.answerText: Resting cartilage, proliferation, hypertrophy, calcification, ossification

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Trace the path of nutrients from a blood vessel in the central canal of an osteon to an osteocyte buried in the matrix. Which order is correct?
options: Perforating canal, then a lamella, then a lacuna
Central canal, then a lacuna, then canaliculi
Central canal, then canaliculi, then a lacuna
A lacuna, then canaliculi, then the central canal
questions.why: Blood vessels run in the central canal at the core of the osteon. From there, nutrients pass outward through canaliculi, the tiny channels that cut through the hard lamellae, until they reach the lacuna where the osteocyte sits. Wastes travel the same route in reverse.
notes: Nutrients cannot pass through a solid lamella, which is a ring of hard matrix. A perforating canal would start the route only if the vessel came in crosswise from another osteon, and canaliculi would still be needed.
This skips the connecting channels. A lacuna is the destination, and nutrients can only reach it through canaliculi, so the lacuna must come last.
Correct. Nutrients move from the central canal through canaliculi to the lacuna.
This is the route in reverse, from the cell to the blood. It would be correct if the question asked how wastes leave an osteocyte.
questions.answerText: Central canal, then canaliculi, then a lacuna

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which list orders the regions of a long bone along a straight line from the joint surface at one end into the shaft?
questions.why: At the joint, articular cartilage caps the end of the bone. Beneath it is the epiphysis, the expanded end filled with spongy bone. Next comes the metaphysis, which holds the growth plate or epiphyseal line, and then the diaphysis, the shaft with the medullary cavity in its center.
notes: Articular cartilage is on the outer joint surface, so nothing in the bone lies outside it. This order also places the shaft before the metaphysis, which reverses their real relationship.
This swaps the epiphysis and metaphysis. The metaphysis is the transition zone between the end and the shaft, so it cannot sit directly under the joint surface.
Correct. Articular cartilage, epiphysis, metaphysis, then diaphysis.
This is the right sequence read in reverse, from the shaft out to the joint. It would be correct if the question started in the diaphysis.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which statement correctly pairs the route that builds the flat bones of the skull with the type of growth that lengthens a long bone?
options: Intramembranous builds them, and appositional growth lengthens a bone
Endochondral builds them, and interstitial growth lengthens a bone
Endochondral builds them, and appositional growth lengthens a bone
Intramembranous builds them, and interstitial growth lengthens a bone
questions.why: The flat bones of the skull form by intramembranous ossification, directly within a connective tissue membrane. Long bones lengthen by interstitial growth, growth from within at the epiphyseal plate. Appositional growth works at the surface and makes bones wider, not longer.
notes: The first half is right, but appositional growth makes a bone wider. This choice would be right only if the question asked how a long bone grows in width.
The growth half is right, but the flat skull bones do not form from a cartilage model. Endochondral ossification would be right for the femur or humerus.

Both halves are wrong here. Endochondral ossification forms most other bones from a cartilage model, and appositional growth widens bones, so this pairing would fit a question about limb bones growing in width.
Correct. Intramembranous for the flat skull bones, interstitial growth for length.
questions.answerText: Intramembranous builds them, and interstitial growth lengthens a bone

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which set correctly names three parts of an osteon: the canal at its center, the rings of matrix around that canal, and the small cavities between those rings?
questions.why: Each osteon has a central canal at its core carrying blood vessels and nerves. Concentric rings of bony matrix, the lamellae, surround the canal. Between the lamellae are small cavities, the lacunae, and each lacuna holds one osteocyte.
notes: Correct. Central canal, lamellae, and lacunae are the three named parts.
The medullary cavity is the marrow space of the whole shaft, not the center of a single osteon. Canaliculi connect lacunae but are not the cavities that hold osteocytes.

A perforating canal runs crosswise between osteons rather than at the center of one, and canaliculi are channels, not cavities. This set would partly fit a question about the connecting passages of compact bone.
Trabeculae are the struts of spongy bone, which has no osteons at all. They would belong in a set describing spongy bone instead.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which statement correctly matches each cartilage type to a structure it forms: the airways, the external ear, and an intervertebral disc?
options: Fibrocartilage for the airways, hyaline for the ear, elastic for the disc
Elastic for the airways, hyaline for the ear, fibrocartilage for the disc
Hyaline for the airways, fibrocartilage for the ear, elastic for the disc
Hyaline for the airways, elastic for the ear, fibrocartilage for the disc
questions.why: Each cartilage type matches the job of its location. Hyaline cartilage, smooth and firm, holds the airways open. Elastic cartilage, packed with elastic fibers, lets the external ear bend and spring back. Fibrocartilage, with thick collagen bundles, absorbs the compression in an intervertebral disc.
notes: This scrambles all three. Fibrocartilage is tough and compression-resistant, which suits a disc, not the airways, and the flexible ear needs elastic cartilage.
This swaps hyaline and elastic cartilage. The airway rings are hyaline, and the springiness of the ear comes from elastic fibers.
The airway match is right, but the ear and the disc are swapped. A disc needs the tough collagen bundles of fibrocartilage, while the bendable ear needs elastic cartilage.
Correct. Hyaline for the airways, elastic for the ear, fibrocartilage for the disc.
questions.answerText: Hyaline for the airways, elastic for the ear, fibrocartilage for the disc

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which list orders the bone cells along a single developmental line, from the stem cell to the cell that maintains mature matrix?
questions.why: The osteogenic cell is the stem cell of bone tissue, and it divides to produce osteoblasts. An osteoblast builds matrix, and once it is surrounded by that matrix it becomes an osteocyte, which maintains the bone day to day. The osteoclast is not part of this line, since it comes from a blood-cell line.
notes: This places the osteoclast in the bone lineage. Osteoclasts come from a blood-cell line and break bone down, so they do not turn into osteocytes.
This is the correct lineage read backward. Mature osteocytes do not turn back into stem cells, so the line runs only from the osteogenic cell forward.
This puts the osteoblast before its own stem cell. The osteogenic cell has to come first because it is the cell that divides to produce osteoblasts.
Correct. Osteogenic cell, then osteoblast, then osteocyte.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: In cartilage, what is the small cavity in the matrix that holds each chondrocyte called?
questions.why: Each chondrocyte sits in a small cavity in the cartilage matrix called a lacuna, which means little lake. Bone uses the same word for the cavity that holds an osteocyte. In cartilage, nutrients reach the chondrocyte by diffusing through the matrix, since cartilage has no blood vessels.
notes: A central canal is the channel at the core of an osteon carrying blood vessels. Cartilage has no central canals, so this choice fits only a compact bone question.
A canaliculus is a tiny channel in bone that links lacunae to each other. It would be the answer for a question about how osteocytes connect, a feature cartilage does not have.
Correct. A chondrocyte sits in a lacuna.
A trabecula is a bony strut of spongy bone. Pick it for a question about the lattice inside the epiphysis.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which bone shape class includes the femur and the humerus?
questions.why: Long bones are longer than they are wide, with a shaft and two ends. The femur of the thigh and the humerus of the arm are the textbook examples. Their shape makes them strong levers for movement.
notes: Irregular bones have complex shapes that fit no other class, like the vertebrae and hip bones. Choose this class for a vertebra.
Short bones are roughly cube-shaped, like the carpals and tarsals. They would be the answer for a question about wrist or ankle bones.
Correct. The femur and humerus are long bones.
Flat bones are thin and often curved, like the sternum, ribs, and most skull bones. Pick this class for broad protective bones.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which bone is the classic example of a sesamoid bone?
questions.why: A sesamoid bone is a small bone that forms within a tendon. The patella, or kneecap, develops inside the tendon of the quadriceps muscle where it crosses the front of the knee. That position lets it protect the tendon and improve the muscle's leverage.
notes: The sternum is a flat bone in the midline of the chest. Choose it for a question about flat bones that protect the heart.
The calcaneus is the heel bone, one of the tarsals, so it is a short bone. Pick it for a question about ankle bones or the bone the calcaneal tendon attaches to.
The scapula is a flat bone, a broad triangular plate on the back of the thorax. It would be the answer for a question about the shoulder blade or a flat bone of the pectoral girdle.
Correct. The patella is the classic sesamoid bone.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: The central canal at the core of an osteon is also known by which eponym?
questions.why: The central canal is also called the Haversian canal, and the whole osteon is called the Haversian system. It runs lengthwise at the core of each osteon and carries blood vessels and nerves. Eponyms like this show up on lab labels, so it helps to pair each one with its plain name.
notes: The nutrient foramen is the opening in the shaft where the nutrient artery enters the bone. Choose it for a question about where the main artery gets into a long bone.
Correct. The central canal is the Haversian canal.
The Volkmann canal is the perforating canal, which runs crosswise and links central canals. It would be the answer if the question asked for the other name of the perforating canal.
Sharpey is the name attached to the perforating fibers, the collagen bundles that anchor the periosteum to bone. There is no Sharpey canal, so this choice mixes up a fiber with a canal.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: What are the concentric rings of bony matrix around the central canal called?
questions.why: Lamellae are the thin rings of bony matrix layered around the central canal of an osteon, like the rings of a tree trunk. These concentric lamellae give the osteon its strength. Lacunae holding osteocytes sit between them.
notes: Correct. The concentric rings around the central canal are lamellae.
Trabeculae are the struts of spongy bone. They would be the answer for a question about the lattice that fills the ends of long bones.
Lacunae are the small cavities between the lamellae that each hold an osteocyte. Choose them for a question about where bone cells sit.
Canaliculi are tiny channels connecting lacunae. Pick them for a question about how osteocytes exchange nutrients and wastes.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: The trabeculae of spongy bone are not arranged randomly. Along what are they aligned?
questions.why: Trabeculae line up along the lines of stress the bone experiences, so each strut carries load in the direction force actually travels. This lets spongy bone stay strong while remaining light. Bone remodels over time, so the pattern shifts if the loads on the bone change.
notes: The periosteum is the outer covering of the bone, lying on compact bone rather than among the trabeculae. Choose it for a question about the membrane on the outer surface.
Spongy bone has no osteons and so no central canals to line up with. This choice mixes up the structure of spongy bone with that of compact bone.

The epiphyseal line is the remnant of the growth plate, a thin band across the bone. Trabeculae pass through that region, but they are oriented by load, not by the line. Pick it for a question about what remains after growth in length ends.
Correct. Trabeculae are aligned along lines of stress.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: An osteoblast becomes surrounded by the matrix it has secreted. Which cell does it become?
questions.why: Osteoblasts build bone by secreting matrix around themselves. Once an osteoblast is fully surrounded, it sits in a lacuna and becomes an osteocyte, a mature bone cell that maintains the matrix day to day. This is the last step of the osteogenic cell to osteoblast to osteocyte lineage.
notes: The osteogenic cell is the stem cell that comes before the osteoblast, so an osteoblast cannot turn back into one. Pick it for a question about the cell that produces osteoblasts.
A chondrocyte is a cartilage cell in a lacuna of cartilage matrix. Choose it for a question about cartilage, since bone cells do not become chondrocytes.
The osteoclast comes from a blood-cell line, not from osteoblasts, and it breaks bone down. It would be the answer for a question about the cell that resorbs bone.
Correct. An osteoblast surrounded by its own matrix becomes an osteocyte.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: In interstitial growth of cartilage, where does the new cartilage come from?
options: Cells of the perichondrium at the surface
questions.why: Cartilage grows in two ways. In interstitial growth, chondrocytes divide inside the matrix and the new cells secrete more matrix, so the cartilage expands from within. Interstitial means within the spaces, which describes growth from the inside out.
notes: Osteoblasts beneath the periosteum add bone, not cartilage, when a bone grows wider. Choose this for a question about appositional growth of bone.
Cells of the perichondrium add cartilage at the outer surface, which is appositional growth. This would be the answer if the question asked about appositional growth.
Correct. Interstitial growth comes from chondrocytes dividing within the matrix.
Osteoclasts break bone down rather than building anything. Pick them for a question about which cell resorbs bone matrix.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: A bone cell maintains the bone matrix day to day from within a lacuna. Which cell is this?
questions.why: Osteocytes are mature bone cells, former osteoblasts that became trapped in the matrix they made. Each sits in its own lacuna and maintains the surrounding matrix, staying connected to its neighbors through canaliculi. They are the most common cells in mature bone.
notes: Correct. The osteocyte maintains the matrix from inside a lacuna.
The osteogenic cell is the stem cell that divides to produce osteoblasts. Choose it for a question about where new bone-building cells come from.
The osteoblast builds new matrix on bone surfaces and is not yet enclosed in a lacuna. It would be the answer for a question about the cell that secretes new bone.
The osteoclast is a large multinucleated cell that resorbs bone. Pick it for a question about the cell that breaks bone down.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Articular cartilage, which caps the ends of bones at a joint, is made of which type of cartilage?
questions.why: Articular cartilage is hyaline cartilage. Its fine collagen fibers give it a smooth, glassy surface, so the bone ends glide over each other with little friction. Like all cartilage it lacks blood vessels, which is why worn joint surfaces heal poorly.
notes: Dense regular connective tissue has parallel collagen fibers and forms tendons and ligaments. Choose it for a question about the tissue connecting muscle to bone.

Fibrocartilage is tough and shock-absorbing, and it forms the menisci inside the knee. Students sometimes choose it for that reason, but the cartilage covering the bone ends themselves is hyaline. Pick fibrocartilage for the menisci or intervertebral discs.
Elastic cartilage is springy and flexible. It would be the answer for the external ear or the epiglottis.
Correct. Articular cartilage is hyaline cartilage.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which type of marrow fills the spaces between the trabeculae of spongy bone in the epiphyses?
questions.why: Red marrow fills the spaces of spongy bone in the epiphyses and is the site of blood cell formation. Yellow marrow, which is mostly stored fat, fills the medullary cavity of the adult shaft. Remembering where each sits helps you place spongy bone at the ends and the marrow cavity in the shaft.
notes: Yellow marrow is fat stored in the medullary cavity of the adult diaphysis. It would be the answer for a question about what fills the hollow core of the shaft.
Hyaline cartilage covers the joint surface and forms the growth plate, but it does not fill the spaces between trabeculae. Pick it for a question about the articular surface.
Compact bone forms the dense outer shell around the spongy bone, not the material inside its spaces. Choose it for a question about the wall of the shaft.
Correct. Red marrow fills the spaces of spongy bone.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which description fits the osteoclast?
options: A cell on the bone surface that secretes matrix
A large cell with many nuclei that resorbs bone
A small cell in a lacuna that maintains matrix
A stem cell that divides to make bone builders
questions.why: The osteoclast is a large, multinucleated cell that breaks down and resorbs bone matrix. It comes from a blood-cell line, unlike the other three bone cells, and it works alongside osteoblasts as bone is constantly reshaped.
notes: This describes the osteoblast, which builds new matrix on bone surfaces. Pick it for a question about the bone-forming cell.
Correct. The osteoclast is large, multinucleated, and resorbs bone.
This describes the osteocyte, a mature bone cell sitting in a lacuna. It would be the answer for a question about the cell that keeps existing matrix healthy.
This describes the osteogenic cell, the stem cell of bone tissue. Choose it for a question about where osteoblasts come from.
questions.answerText: A large cell with many nuclei that resorbs bone

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: During endochondral ossification, bone replaces a model made of which tissue?
questions.why: In endochondral ossification, a model of the future bone is first laid down in hyaline cartilage. Bone then gradually replaces that cartilage, and the last cartilage left in a growing long bone is at the epiphyseal plate and the articular surface. Most bones of the body form this way.
notes: Fibrocartilage forms the intervertebral discs and menisci and is not the model for developing bones. Pick it for a question about shock-absorbing pads.
A fibrous connective tissue membrane is the starting tissue for intramembranous ossification. Choose it for a question about how the flat bones of the skull form.
Correct. Endochondral ossification replaces a hyaline cartilage model.
Elastic cartilage stays as cartilage in the external ear and epiglottis and is not replaced by bone. It would be the answer for a question about those flexible structures.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: The growth plate shows up as a gap on a child's X-ray. Why does it look like a gap?
options: It is the medullary cavity filled with marrow
It is cartilage, which is not mineralized like bone
It is a fracture line that has not yet healed
It is a space left where osteoclasts removed bone
questions.why: X-rays show mineralized bone clearly, while unmineralized tissue such as cartilage lets the beam pass and looks dark. The epiphyseal plate is a disc of hyaline cartilage, so it appears as a gap between the shaft and the end of the bone. Once growth ends and bone replaces the plate, the gap is gone and a thin epiphyseal line remains.
notes: The medullary cavity runs lengthwise inside the shaft, not across the bone near its end. Pick it for a question about where yellow marrow is stored.
Correct. The plate is cartilage, so it does not show like mineralized bone.

A fracture can also appear as a dark line, which is why students confuse the two. A growth plate sits in a predictable spot at the metaphysis, so this choice would only fit an irregular break line after an injury.
Osteoclasts resorb bone in small areas during remodeling, but they do not create a band across the bone. This choice mixes up normal growth cartilage with bone loss.
questions.answerText: It is cartilage, which is not mineralized like bone

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: An adult X-ray shows an epiphyseal line at the end of a long bone. What does this finding tell the clinician?
options: The bone is being resorbed by osteoclasts
The bone is still growing in length
The bone has a recent fracture across its end
questions.why: The epiphyseal line is the bony remnant of the growth plate. It forms when the cartilage of the plate has been fully replaced by bone at the end of growth in length. Seeing a line instead of a cartilage gap tells the clinician the skeleton is mature.
notes: Correct. An epiphyseal line means the plate has closed.
Osteoclasts remodel bone throughout life, but that process does not produce the epiphyseal line. Pick resorption for a question about loss of bone density, not a normal growth landmark.
An actively growing bone would show the epiphyseal plate as a cartilage gap. This choice would be right if the X-ray showed a gap rather than a line.
A fracture line is irregular and follows the injury, while the epiphyseal line sits in a fixed position at the metaphysis. This choice confuses a normal landmark with an injury.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: A long bone tends to break under a twisting force rather than a force along its length. Which structural feature explains this?
options: Its osteons are aligned with the long axis
It is made entirely of spongy bone
Its osteons lie across the long axis
questions.why: The osteons of compact bone run parallel to the long axis of the bone, along the lines of stress it normally carries. That makes a long bone very strong against forces along its length, such as body weight. A twisting force acts off that axis, against the grain of the osteons, so it is the force most likely to cause a break.
notes: Correct. Osteons run with the long axis, so twisting forces off that axis are the dangerous ones.
The shaft of a long bone is compact bone, with spongy bone mainly in the epiphyses. This choice would describe the inside of the bone ends, not the shaft.
This reverses the real arrangement. Osteons run lengthwise along the shaft, in line with the body weight the bone normally carries, not across it.
Long bones do have perforating canals, which carry vessels crosswise between osteons. This choice treats a blood vessel channel as a strength feature, which it is not.
questions.answerText: Its osteons are aligned with the long axis

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: The five zones of the growth plate run from the epiphysis to the diaphysis. Which zone lies closest to the epiphysis?
questions.why: The zone of resting cartilage is the first zone, sitting right against the epiphysis. Its job is to anchor the growth plate to the epiphysis. Moving toward the shaft, the cells divide, enlarge, calcify, and are finally replaced by bone in the zone of ossification beside the diaphysis.
notes: The zone of hypertrophy is the third zone, where chondrocytes enlarge. Pick it for a question about where the cartilage cells swell.
Correct. The zone of resting cartilage lies closest to the epiphysis and anchors the plate.
The zone of calcification is the fourth zone, where the cartilage matrix hardens. Choose it for a question about where the matrix calcifies just before bone forms.
The zone of ossification is the last zone, next to the diaphysis, where bone replaces the cartilage. It would be the answer if the question asked which zone is closest to the shaft.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: A child breaks a bone, and the fracture runs through the growth plate. Why do clinicians describe pediatric fractures by how they cross the plate?
options: The plate is the strongest region of a child's bone
Breaks through the plate always heal faster than others
The plate is where the nutrient artery enters the bone
A break through the plate can slow or stop growth in length
questions.why: The epiphyseal plate is where a long bone grows in length. If a fracture damages the plate, that growth can slow or stop, which may leave the limb shorter or crooked. Describing the fracture by how it crosses the plate tells the care team how much risk there is to future growth.
notes: The plate is cartilage, which is weaker than the bone around it, so it is actually a common site of injury in children. This choice reverses the real situation.
There is no rule that growth plate fractures heal faster, and cartilage generally heals slowly. This choice ignores the real concern, which is future growth.
The nutrient artery enters through the nutrient foramen in the shaft, not at the growth plate. Pick the nutrient foramen for a question about how the main artery reaches the marrow.
Correct. Damage to the plate can disturb growth in length.
questions.answerText: A break through the plate can slow or stop growth in length

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Compact bone is built from osteons, each with a central canal. Why does each osteon need a canal at its core?
options: It stores yellow marrow for each individual osteon
It brings blood vessels to the buried osteocytes
It holds the single osteocyte that maintains the osteon
It anchors the periosteum firmly to the bone surface
questions.why: Mineralized bone matrix is too hard and dense for nutrients to diffuse through it. The central canal brings blood vessels (and nerves) right into the middle of each osteon, and canaliculi carry nutrients from there out to the osteocytes in their lacunae. Without that core blood supply, the cells deep in compact bone would die.
notes: Yellow marrow is stored in the medullary cavity of the shaft, not inside individual osteons. Pick the medullary cavity for a question about where fat is stored in a long bone.
Correct. The central canal brings a blood supply to the osteocytes.
Each osteon contains many osteocytes, each sitting in its own lacuna between the lamellae. Pick the lacuna for a question about where a single bone cell lives.
Perforating (Sharpey) fibers, bundles of collagen, are what anchor the periosteum to the bone. Choose them for a question about how the outer membrane stays attached.
questions.answerText: It brings blood vessels to the buried osteocytes

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Spongy bone fills the ends of long bones, while compact bone forms the walls of the shaft. Why does spongy bone suit the ends?
options: It is denser than compact bone, so it adds the most strength
The ends carry no load, so a weaker tissue is enough
Its trabeculae give strength with less weight
It contains the growth plate, so it lets the bone lengthen
questions.why: The ends of long bones receive forces from several directions at the joint. Spongy bone handles this with trabeculae, struts aligned along the lines of stress, so it is strong where force travels while staying light. Its spaces also hold red marrow, the site of blood cell formation.
notes: Spongy bone is lighter and less dense than compact bone, not denser. This choice reverses the two tissues.
The ends of long bones carry large loads at every joint. This choice mistakes the lighter design of spongy bone for weakness.
Correct. Trabeculae aligned with stress give strength at low weight.

The growth plate is a separate cartilage disc in the metaphysis, and it is the cartilage, not the spongy bone, that allows lengthening. Pick the epiphyseal plate for a question about where length is added.
questions.answerText: Its trabeculae give strength with less weight

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Bone is constantly remodeled, with osteoblasts building and osteoclasts breaking down. Why is ongoing breakdown, not just building, part of healthy bone?
options: It lets bone repair, reshape, and release calcium
Osteoclasts build new bone, so more breakdown adds bone mass
Osteoclasts turn into osteoblasts once they finish resorbing
Breakdown happens only in disease and not in healthy bone
questions.why: Remodeling pairs osteoclasts, which remove old or damaged matrix, with osteoblasts, which lay down new matrix in its place. This lets bone repair tiny cracks, reshape itself to the loads it carries, and release calcium it stores when the body needs it. Building alone could only add bone, never correct or reshape it.
notes: Correct. Breakdown is half of a repair and reshaping cycle.
This swaps the cell roles. Osteoclasts resorb bone, and osteoblasts are the builders, so this choice would be right only if the names were reversed.
Osteoclasts come from a blood-cell line and do not become osteoblasts. Osteoblasts come from osteogenic cells, so this choice mixes up the two lineages.
Osteoclasts are active in healthy bone every day. This choice confuses normal remodeling with disease, where breakdown outpaces building.
questions.answerText: It lets bone repair, reshape, and release calcium

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Osteocytes sit in lacunae and connect through thin channels called canaliculi. Why are the canaliculi essential to osteocyte survival?
options: They carry blood vessels deep into the center of the osteon
They let nutrients and wastes move between cells and blood vessels
They store calcium crystals away from the osteocytes
They hold the osteocytes in place between the lamellae
questions.why: Bone matrix is mineralized and too dense for nutrients to diffuse through. Canaliculi are tiny channels that run from lacuna to lacuna and back to the central canal, where the blood vessels are. Osteocytes extend thin processes through these channels and pass nutrients and wastes cell to cell.
notes: Blood vessels run in the central canal and in perforating canals, which are much larger than canaliculi. Pick the central canal for a question about where the osteon's vessels run.
Correct. Canaliculi are the supply lines between the osteocytes and the blood.
Calcium is stored in the mineralized matrix itself, not in the canaliculi. This choice mixes up a channel with the mineral store of bone.
Lacunae are the cavities that hold each osteocyte in place. Choose the lacuna for a question about where an osteocyte sits.
questions.answerText: They let nutrients and wastes move between cells and blood vessels

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: The organic part of bone matrix is mostly collagen, and the inorganic part is mostly calcium mineral. Why does bone need both?
options: Both resist only compression, so either one alone would work
Collagen anchors the periosteum, while mineral lines the marrow cavity
Collagen resists tension and bending, while mineral resists compression
Mineral provides flexibility, while collagen provides hardness
questions.why: Collagen fibers give bone some flexibility and resistance to pulling and bending forces, while calcium mineral makes it hard and resistant to crushing. Bone with too little mineral bends too easily, and bone with too little collagen becomes brittle and snaps. Together they make a tissue that is both hard and tough.
notes: The two components resist different forces. If either one alone were enough, bone would not become brittle when collagen is lacking or soft when mineral is lacking.

Perforating fibers made of collagen do anchor the periosteum, but that is not why collagen is in the matrix itself, and mineral does not line the marrow cavity. The endosteum is what lines the cavity.
Correct. Collagen handles tension, and mineral handles compression.
This reverses the two components. Mineral is the hard part of the matrix, and collagen supplies the flexibility.
questions.answerText: Collagen resists tension and bending, while mineral resists compression

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: In a child the epiphyseal plate is cartilage, and in an adult it becomes a bony line. Why must the plate be cartilage while the bone is growing in length?
options: Cartilage carries the blood supply to the growing bone end
Bone can expand from within its matrix as easily as cartilage
Cartilage can grow from within and then be replaced by bone
Cartilage is stronger than bone at bearing body weight
questions.why: Cartilage can grow interstitially, meaning its cells divide and expand the tissue from within. At the growth plate, new cartilage keeps forming on the epiphysis side while bone replaces older cartilage on the shaft side, so the bone lengthens. Hard bone matrix cannot expand from within, which is why the plate has to stay cartilage until growth ends.
notes: Cartilage has no blood vessels of its own, so it cannot be the blood supply for anything. This choice ignores one of cartilage's defining features.
Bone can only add matrix at its surfaces, not swell from within, because its matrix is mineralized. That limitation is exactly why lengthening needs a cartilage plate.
Correct. Cartilage grows from within and is then replaced by bone.
Cartilage is actually weaker than bone, which is why growth plates are a common fracture site in children. This choice reverses their strength.
questions.answerText: Cartilage can grow from within and then be replaced by bone

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: A weight lifter's bones become denser over years of training. Why does repeated mechanical stress increase bone density?
options: Loading reopens the epiphyseal plates so adult bones grow
Loading turns the cartilage of the growth plate into new bone
Osteoblasts add matrix where stress is high
Loading makes osteoclasts switch to building new matrix
questions.why: Bone is living tissue that is constantly remodeled. When a bone carries more load, osteoblasts add matrix where stress is greatest and the trabeculae realign along the new stress lines, so the bone becomes denser and stronger. When load is removed, as in long bed rest, the balance shifts the other way and bone is lost.
notes: Closed epiphyseal plates do not reopen, and adult bones do not grow longer with training. Density increases, not length.
In an adult the growth plate has already closed into the epiphyseal line, so there is no plate cartilage left to convert. This choice confuses growth in childhood with adaptation in adults.
Correct. Bone adapts to load through remodeling.
Osteoclasts always resorb bone; they do not switch to building. The building is done by osteoblasts, so this choice swaps the cell roles.
questions.answerText: Osteoblasts add matrix where stress is high

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: After a fracture, a soft cartilage callus forms first and is later replaced by bone. Why does the body build cartilage before bone?
options: Osteoclasts build the cartilage callus, which only they can make
The cartilage callus lengthens the bone to make up for the break
Cartilage can form without a blood supply and bridges the gap first
Cartilage is the permanent repair tissue and stays in place
questions.why: A fracture tears the blood vessels at the break, leaving the area with a poor blood supply at first. Cartilage does not need blood vessels of its own, so it can form a callus that bridges the bone ends early. As new vessels grow in, the cartilage is replaced by bone, much as bone replaces cartilage during endochondral ossification.
notes: Osteoclasts resorb bone and play no part in making cartilage. The callus cartilage is made by chondrocytes that develop at the fracture site.
The callus joins the broken ends; it does not add length. Growth in length happens only at an open epiphyseal plate.
Correct. Avascular cartilage can bridge the break before blood supply returns.
The cartilage callus is temporary and is replaced by a bony callus that is later remodeled. This choice stops the repair story too early.
questions.answerText: Cartilage can form without a blood supply and bridges the gap first

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: The flat bones of the skull ossify directly within a fibrous membrane, while long bones form from a cartilage model. How does each route suit each bone?
options: The route a bone takes has no link to its shape or growth
Long bones form in membranes so they can widen; skull bones need cartilage
Skull bones need a cartilage model so that they can grow in length
Skull plates form directly as sheets; long bones need cartilage to lengthen
questions.why: The flat skull bones are thin protective plates, and intramembranous ossification builds them directly as sheets inside a membrane, without a cartilage stage. Long bones form by endochondral ossification from a hyaline cartilage model, and the cartilage that remains at the epiphyseal plates lets them keep growing in length through childhood.
notes: The two routes do match the bones they build: flat sheets from membranes, and growing levers from cartilage models with growth plates. This choice misses that link.
This swaps the two routes. Long bones are the ones with a cartilage model, and the skull's flat bones form in membranes.
Flat skull bones form without a cartilage model, and they do not lengthen at growth plates the way long bones do. This choice applies the long bone pattern to the skull.
Correct. Each route matches the shape and growth needs of the bone.
questions.answerText: Skull plates form directly as sheets; long bones need cartilage to lengthen

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which lamellae run around the entire outer and inner circumference of the shaft, deep to the periosteum and around the medullary cavity?
questions.why: Circumferential lamellae are layers of bone that wrap the entire outer surface of the shaft, just under the periosteum, and the entire inner surface around the medullary cavity. They belong to the whole bone rather than to any single osteon. The name comes from circumference, the distance around a circle.
notes: Correct. Circumferential lamellae wrap the whole shaft inside and out.
Trabeculae are the struts of spongy bone, not layers of compact bone. Choose them for a question about the lattice inside the epiphysis.
Interstitial lamellae are leftover fragments of old osteons filling the gaps between intact ones. Pick them for a question about the partial rings between osteons.
Concentric lamellae are the rings around the central canal of one osteon. They would be the answer for a question about the layers of a single osteon.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: What are the incomplete lamellae wedged between intact osteons, left over from old osteons during remodeling, called?
questions.why: Interstitial lamellae are fragments of older osteons that were partly broken down during remodeling. They fill the irregular gaps between the intact osteons. Interstitial means in between, which matches where they sit.
notes: Correct. The leftover fragments between osteons are interstitial lamellae.
Concentric lamellae are the complete rings around a central canal. They would be the answer for a question about the rings of a whole osteon.
Trabeculae are the struts of spongy bone. Choose them for a question about the lattice in the ends of long bones.
Circumferential lamellae wrap the outer and inner surfaces of the shaft. Pick them for a question about the layers just beneath the periosteum.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: A compact bone slide shows complete rings around a central canal, partial fragments between those units, and layers wrapping the bone's outer edge. Which list names these lamellae in that order?
questions.why: Complete rings around a central canal are concentric lamellae, the rings of an osteon. The partial fragments between osteons are interstitial lamellae, left from older osteons. Layers wrapping the whole outer or inner surface of the shaft are circumferential lamellae.
notes: This swaps the first two. The complete rings of an osteon are concentric lamellae, and the fragments between osteons are interstitial lamellae.
This reverses the first and last terms. Circumferential lamellae wrap the edge of the bone, so they match the third description, not the first.
Correct. Concentric, interstitial, then circumferential.
This swaps the last two. Fragments between osteons are interstitial, and the layers around the bone's edge are circumferential.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which bone shape class includes the sternum, the ribs, and most skull bones?
questions.why: Flat bones are thin and often curved. The sternum, the ribs, and most bones of the skull are flat bones. Their broad, plate-like shape makes them good at protecting organs, such as the brain in the cranium and the heart and lungs in the thoracic cage.
notes: Correct. The sternum, ribs, and most skull bones are flat bones.
Long bones are longer than they are wide, with a shaft and two ends, like the femur and humerus. They would be the answer for a question about the bones of the limbs.
Irregular bones have complex shapes that fit no other class, like the vertebrae and hip bones. Choose this class for a question about a vertebra.
Short bones are roughly cube-shaped, like the carpals and tarsals. Pick this class for a question about wrist and ankle bones.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: Which bone shape class includes the vertebrae and the hip bones?
questions.why: Irregular bones have complex shapes that do not fit the long, short, flat, or sesamoid groups. The vertebrae, with their bodies, arches, and processes, and the hip bones are the standard examples. Their shapes reflect the many muscles, joints, and openings they have to accommodate.
notes: Sesamoid bones are small bones formed within a tendon, like the patella. Pick this class for a question about the kneecap.
Flat bones are thin, often curved plates such as the sternum, ribs, and most skull bones. They would be the answer for a question about the bones that roof the cranium.
Short bones are roughly cube-shaped, like the carpals and tarsals. Choose this class for a question about wrist or ankle bones.
Correct. The vertebrae and hip bones are irregular bones.

questions.topic: Bone tissue, the long bone and bone microanatomy
questions.q: What anchors the periosteum firmly into the underlying bone?
questions.why: Perforating fibers, also called Sharpey fibers, are bundles of collagen that run from the periosteum into the underlying bone matrix. They pin the periosteum tightly to the bone surface. This firm attachment matters because tendons and ligaments pull on bone through the periosteum.
notes: Correct. Perforating (Sharpey) fibers anchor the periosteum.

Circumferential lamellae are layers of bone just under the periosteum, wrapping the shaft. They lie beneath the periosteum, but they are bone layers, not the fibers that tie it down. Choose them for a question about the outer layers of compact bone.
