Correct. The trochlea meets the ulna, the medial epicondyle sits above it, and the ulnar nerve passes behind it.
questions.answerText: The medial epicondyle, with the ulnar nerve behind it.

questions.topic: Pectoral girdle and upper limb bones
questions.q: In lab, a student holds a loose forearm bone. Its proximal end is a disc-shaped head, and its distal end has a styloid process on one side and a notch on the other. Which bone is it, and which humeral marking does its head meet?
options: The radius; its head meets the capitulum.
The ulna; its head meets the trochlea.
The radius; its head meets the trochlea.
The ulna; its head meets the capitulum.
questions.why: Name the bone from its ends. A disc-shaped head at the proximal end and an ulnar notch at the distal end belong to the radius, the lateral forearm bone. At the elbow, the radial head articulates with the capitulum, the lateral knob of the distal humerus.
notes: Correct. A disc-shaped proximal head belongs to the radius, which meets the capitulum.
The ulna's elbow end is the olecranon and trochlear notch, which grip the trochlea. Its head is at the wrist end, not the elbow.
The bone is right, but the trochlea is the medial spool that meets the ulna. The radius meets the lateral capitulum.
The capitulum meets the radius, not the ulna. A disc-shaped proximal head is the radial head.
questions.answerText: The radius; its head meets the capitulum.

questions.topic: Pectoral girdle and upper limb bones
questions.q: On an articulated wrist, a student puts a finger on the carpal most often dislocated, then moves one bone toward the little finger within the same row. Which bone is the student touching now?
questions.why: Two steps get you there. The carpal most often dislocated is the lunate, the second bone of the proximal row. The proximal row runs scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform from the thumb side (So Long To Pinky), so one bone toward the little finger is the triquetrum.
notes: Correct. The lunate is most often dislocated, and the next bone toward the little finger in the proximal row is the triquetrum.
The scaphoid is next to the lunate, but on the thumb side. It is the carpal most often fractured.
The pisiform is the last bone of the proximal row on the little-finger side, two bones from the lunate, not one.
The capitate is the largest carpal and sits in the distal row. The student stayed in the proximal row.

questions.topic: Pectoral girdle and upper limb bones
questions.q: In bone-marking vocabulary, what is a sulcus?
questions.why: A sulcus is a groove in a bone, one of the depression markings. The intertubercular sulcus of the humerus, the groove between the tubercles that holds a biceps tendon, is the standard example.
notes: A shallow basin is a fossa, such as the olecranon fossa. It is a depression, but not a groove.
A small rounded bump is a tubercle, a projection. A sulcus dips into the bone instead.
A hole for vessels or nerves is a foramen, an opening. A sulcus is a groove that does not pass through the bone.
Correct. A sulcus is a groove, a type of depression.

questions.topic: Pectoral girdle and upper limb bones
questions.q: Which bone-marking term names a raised area above a condyle?
questions.why: An epicondyle is a projection that sits just above a condyle. The medial epicondyle of the humerus is the standard example, and the femur has medial and lateral epicondyles above its condyles.
notes: A tubercle is a small rounded bump, like the greater tubercle of the humerus. It is not defined by sitting above a condyle.
A facet is a smooth, nearly flat articular surface, like the articular facets of vertebrae. It is not a raised area.
A head is a bony expansion carried on a neck, like the head of the humerus. It is defined by the neck below it, not by sitting above a condyle.
Correct. An epicondyle is a raised area above a condyle.

questions.topic: Pectoral girdle and upper limb bones
questions.q: The deltoid tuberosity, the mandibular fossa, and the mental foramen are three bone markings. Which list classifies them in that order?
questions.why: Classify each by its term. A tuberosity is a large rough projection. A fossa is a shallow basin, which makes it a depression. A foramen is a hole for vessels or nerves, which makes it an opening.
notes: Correct. A tuberosity is a projection, a fossa is a depression, and a foramen is an opening.
This swaps the last two. A fossa is a shallow basin, a depression, and a foramen is a hole, an opening.
A tuberosity is not a depression. It is a large rough projection where a muscle attaches.
A foramen is not a depression. It passes through the bone, which makes it an opening.

questions.topic: Pectoral girdle and upper limb bones
questions.q: Which of these bone markings is a depression?
questions.why: Depressions dip into the bone without passing through it, and the two depression terms are fossa and sulcus. The intertubercular sulcus is a groove between the tubercles of the humerus, so it is a depression.
notes: A tubercle is a small rounded bump, so the greater tubercle is a projection.
A process is any bony prominence, so the mastoid process is a projection.
A foramen is a hole for vessels or nerves, so it is an opening rather than a depression.
Correct. A sulcus is a groove, which makes it a depression.

questions.topic: Pectoral girdle and upper limb bones
questions.q: Where one vertebra meets the next, the joining surfaces are smooth and nearly flat. Which kind of marking is this?
questions.why: A facet is a smooth, nearly flat articular surface where one bone meets another. The articular facets of the vertebrae, on their articular processes, are the standard example.
notes: A fossa is a shallow basin, such as the olecranon fossa. The vertebral joint surfaces are nearly flat, not basins.
Correct. A smooth, nearly flat surface is a facet, an articular surface.
A tubercle is a small rounded bump. A flat joining surface is a facet.
A sulcus is a groove, such as the intertubercular sulcus. A flat joint surface is not a groove.

questions.topic: Pectoral girdle and upper limb bones
questions.q: A student reads lateral epicondyle of the femur on the lab list. Before finding it, what can the student predict about it from the term alone?
options: It is a groove beside the lateral condyle that holds a tendon.
It is a hole in the lateral condyle that passes a nerve.
It projects just above the lateral condyle, the knob meeting the tibia.
It is a basin below the lateral condyle that receives the patella.
questions.why: Use the term to predict the structure. An epicondyle is a projection, a raised area above a condyle. On the femur, the medial and lateral condyles are the rounded distal knobs that articulate with the tibia, so the lateral epicondyle should project just above the lateral condyle.
notes: A groove is a sulcus, a depression. An epicondyle is a projection.
A hole for vessels or nerves is a foramen, an opening. An epicondyle is a raised area.
Correct. An epicondyle is a raised area above a condyle, and the femoral condyles meet the tibia.
A basin is a fossa, a depression, and an epicondyle sits above a condyle, not below it. The patella glides on the patellar surface of the femur.
questions.answerText: It projects just above the lateral condyle, the knob meeting the tibia.

questions.topic: Pectoral girdle and upper limb bones
questions.q: The term head is used for the proximal ends of both the humerus and the femur. What earns both the name, and what lies just below each head?
options: Each is a large rough projection, so a tuberosity lies below.
Each is an expansion carried on a neck, so a neck lies below.
Each is a smooth flat facet, so a sulcus lies below.
Each is a shallow basin, so a foramen lies below.
questions.why: A head is defined as a bony expansion carried on a neck. The head of the humerus sits on the anatomical neck, and the head of the femur sits on the femoral neck, so the term predicts a narrower neck just below each head.
notes: A large rough projection is a tuberosity. A head is smooth and rounded, carried on a neck.
Correct. A head is a bony expansion carried on a neck, and both bones have a neck below the head.
A facet is nearly flat, and both heads are rounded. What lies below each head is a neck.
A shallow basin is a fossa, a depression. A head is a projection, not a basin.
questions.answerText: Each is an expansion carried on a neck, so a neck lies below.

questions.topic: Pectoral girdle and upper limb bones
questions.q: On a humerus, a student points to the groove between the tubercles and to the hole in the shaft where the artery enters. The student labels both as depressions. Which correction is right?
options: The groove is a depression, but the hole is a foramen, an opening.
Both are openings, since a groove is a long foramen.
The hole is a fossa and the groove is a facet.
The groove is a tubercle, a projection, and the hole is a fossa.
questions.why: Name each marking, then classify it. The groove between the tubercles is the intertubercular sulcus, and a sulcus is a depression. The hole where the nutrient artery enters is the nutrient foramen, and a foramen passes through the bone, so it is an opening.
notes: Correct. The intertubercular sulcus is a depression, but the nutrient foramen is an opening.
A groove does not pass through the bone. The intertubercular sulcus is a depression.
A fossa is a shallow basin and a facet is a smooth flat joint surface. The hole is a foramen and the groove is a sulcus.
The tubercles are the bumps on either side of the groove, not the groove itself, and a hole is a foramen.
questions.answerText: The groove is a depression, but the hole is a foramen, an opening.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which three bones fuse to form each hip bone?
options: The ilium, the ischium, and the pubis
The ilium, the sacrum, and the pubis
The ischium, the pubis, and the coccyx
The ilium, the ischium, and the femur
questions.why: Each hip bone, also called the os coxae or coxal bone, starts out as three separate bones: the ilium on top, the ischium at the back and bottom, and the pubis in front. These three fuse together at the acetabulum, the socket that holds the head of the femur. The sacrum and coccyx join the two hip bones to complete the pelvis, but they are not part of the hip bone itself.
notes: Correct. The ilium, ischium, and pubis fuse at the acetabulum to form one hip bone.

The ilium and pubis are correct, but the sacrum is an axial bone formed from fused vertebrae. It joins the ilium at the sacroiliac joint, so it is a neighbor of the hip bone rather than one of its parts. The sacrum would fit a question about which bones complete the bony pelvis.

The ischium and pubis are correct, but the coccyx is the tailbone at the bottom of the vertebral column. Choose the coccyx if the question asked for the small axial bone that, along with the sacrum, completes the bony pelvis.

The ilium and ischium are correct, but the femur is the thigh bone, a separate bone whose head sits in the acetabulum. Students pick this when they blur the hip bone with the hip joint, which includes the femur.
questions.answerText: The ilium, the ischium, and the pubis

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: What is the common name for the femur?
questions.why: The femur is the thigh bone, the single bone that spans the region from the hip to the knee. It is the longest and strongest bone in the body because it carries the body's weight from the pelvis down to the leg. Its head fits into the acetabulum at the hip, and its condyles meet the tibia at the knee.
notes: The kneecap is the patella, a sesamoid bone that sits in front of the knee within the quadriceps tendon. It is the answer if the question asked what the patella is commonly called.
The shin bone is the tibia, the medial bone of the leg between the knee and the ankle. It would be the answer if the question asked for the common name of the tibia.
Correct. The femur is the thigh bone, the only bone between the hip and the knee.
The heel bone is the calcaneus, the largest tarsal bone at the back of the foot. Pick it if the question asked for the common name of the calcaneus.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which bone is the kneecap?
questions.why: The kneecap is the patella, a sesamoid bone, meaning a bone that forms inside a tendon. It develops within the quadriceps tendon and sits in front of the knee, where it glides over the patellar surface of the femur. Below it, the patellar ligament continues down to the tibial tuberosity.
notes: Correct. The patella is the kneecap, a sesamoid bone in the quadriceps tendon.
The navicular is a boat-shaped tarsal on the medial side of the foot, between the talus and the cuneiforms. It would fit a question about the tarsal just in front of the talus.
The calcaneus is the heel bone, the largest tarsal. Choose it if the question asked which bone forms the heel.

The talus is the tarsal bone at the ankle that articulates with the tibia and fibula and receives the body's weight from the leg. It would be the answer for the ankle bone that sits on top of the calcaneus.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: How many tarsal bones form the ankle and the back of the foot?
questions.why: There are seven tarsal bones in each foot: the talus, the calcaneus, the navicular, the cuboid, and three cuneiforms (medial, intermediate, and lateral). Together they form the ankle and the posterior half of the foot. The talus carries the body's weight from the leg, and the calcaneus forms the heel.
notes: Five is the number of metatarsals, the bones of the sole between the tarsals and the toes. It would be right if the question asked how many metatarsals are in one foot.
Eight is the number of carpal bones in the wrist. Students who mirror the hand onto the foot pick it, but the foot has one fewer tarsal than the hand has carpals.
Correct. Each foot has seven tarsals.
Fourteen is the number of phalanges in one foot, the toe bones. Pick it if the question asked how many phalanges are in each foot.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: What is the deep cup of the hip bone that receives the head of the femur called?
questions.why: The acetabulum is the deep, cup-shaped socket on the lateral side of the hip bone. It is the spot where the ilium, ischium, and pubis fuse, and it receives the head of the femur to form the hip joint. Because the socket is deep, the hip is much more stable than the shoulder.
notes: The greater sciatic notch is a deep notch on the posterior border of the ilium that the sciatic nerve passes through. It would be the answer if the question asked where the largest nerve in the body leaves the pelvis.

The obturator foramen is the large opening below the acetabulum, framed by the ischium and the pubis. It is a hole through the bone, not a socket, and it would be the answer for the largest opening in the hip bone.
Correct. The acetabulum is the socket that receives the femoral head.

The iliac fossa is the smooth, concave inner surface of the ilium, facing the abdomen. It is shallow and does not articulate with any bone. Pick it if the question asked about the inner surface of the ilium.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which two bones form the leg, the region from the knee to the ankle?
questions.why: In anatomy, the leg is only the region between the knee and the ankle, and it contains two bones. The tibia is the thick, medial, weight-bearing shin bone, and the fibula is the slender lateral bone that does not bear body weight. The thigh, above the knee, is a separate region with the femur as its only long bone.
notes: Correct. The tibia and fibula are the two bones of the leg.
The femur and tibia meet at the knee joint, but only the tibia is in the leg. This pair would fit a question about which bones form the tibiofemoral joint.
The talus and calcaneus are tarsal bones of the foot, below the ankle. Pick them if the question asked for the two largest tarsals or the bones of the heel and ankle.
The femur and patella belong to the thigh and knee, above the leg. They would be the answer if the question asked which bones are found in the thigh region from hip to knee.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which tarsal bone is the heel bone and the largest tarsal?
questions.why: The calcaneus is the heel bone and the largest of the seven tarsals. It sits under the talus and projects backward, where it takes the impact of each heel strike and anchors the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon. The talus above it is the bone that receives weight directly from the tibia.
notes: The talus is the tarsal that sits on top of the calcaneus and articulates with the tibia and fibula. It would be the answer for the tarsal that receives the body's weight from the leg.
Correct. The calcaneus is the heel bone and the largest tarsal.

The cuboid is a cube-shaped tarsal on the lateral side of the foot, in front of the calcaneus. Choose it if the question asked which tarsal lies on the lateral side, in line with the fourth and fifth metatarsals.
The navicular is a boat-shaped tarsal on the medial side, between the talus and the three cuneiforms. It would fit a question about the tarsal directly in front of the talus.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: What is the large lateral projection at the proximal end of the femur called?
questions.why: The greater trochanter is the large bump on the lateral side of the proximal femur, just beyond the neck. It is a major attachment site for hip muscles, and you can feel it on the side of your hip. Its smaller partner, the lesser trochanter, sits on the medial side a little lower down.
notes: The fovea capitis is the small pit on the femoral head that anchors a ligament to the acetabulum. Choose it if the question asked about the pit on the head of the femur.

The linea aspera is the rough ridge running down the posterior shaft of the femur, an attachment line for thigh muscles. It would be the answer if the question asked about the back of the femoral shaft.
Correct. The greater trochanter is the large lateral projection near the top of the femur.
The lesser trochanter is the smaller projection on the medial side of the proximal femur, below the neck. Pick it if the question asked for the small medial projection.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: How many phalanges are in one human foot?
questions.why: Each foot has fourteen phalanges. The great toe, the hallux, has only two (a proximal and a distal phalanx), and each of the other four toes has three (proximal, middle, and distal). That gives 2 plus 4 times 3, which is fourteen, the same count as in the hand.
notes: Seven is the number of tarsal bones in each foot. Pick it if the question asked how many bones form the ankle and back of the foot.
Correct. The foot has fourteen phalanges: two in the hallux and three in each other toe.
Ten would be the count if every toe had only two phalanges, like the great toe. Students who generalize the hallux to all the toes land on this number.
Five is the number of metatarsals, one behind each toe. It would be right if the question asked how many metatarsals are in one foot.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: What is the curved upper ridge of the ilium, the rim you rest your hands on, called?
questions.why: The iliac crest is the curved superior border of the ilium. When you put your hands on your hips, they rest on this ridge. It ends in front at the anterior superior iliac spine and in back at the posterior superior iliac spine, and clinicians use it as a landmark they can feel through the skin.
notes: The pubic crest is the ridge along the upper border of the pubis, at the front of the pelvis near the midline. It would be the answer if the question asked about the ridge on the pubis.
Correct. The iliac crest is the curved upper ridge of the ilium.
The ischial tuberosity is the roughened knob of the ischium that you sit on. It would fit a question about the part of the hip bone that bears weight when sitting.
The iliac fossa is the smooth, concave inner surface of the ilium, not its upper rim. Pick it if the question asked for the shallow depression on the inside of the ilium.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: What is the anatomical name for the great toe?
questions.why: The great toe is called the hallux. It is digit I of the foot, and it has only two phalanges, a proximal and a distal, while toes 2 to 5 have three. Metatarsal I sits directly behind it.
notes: The pollex is the thumb, the matching digit I of the hand. Students mix the two up because both are the first digit with only two phalanges. Pick the pollex if the question asked about the hand.
The digitus minimus is the little digit, the fifth toe or the fifth finger. It would be the answer if the question asked for the anatomical name of the smallest toe.
Correct. The hallux is the great toe.
The calcaneus is the heel bone, a tarsal, not a toe at all. Choose it if the question asked which bone forms the heel.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: What is the rough ridge running down the posterior shaft of the femur called?
questions.why: The linea aspera, which means rough line, is a raised ridge along the back of the femoral shaft. It has a medial and a lateral lip and serves as an attachment line for many thigh muscles, including the adductors. Near the distal end its lips split into the medial and lateral supracondylar lines.
notes: The fovea capitis is the small pit on the head of the femur. It would be the answer for the depression where a ligament anchors the femoral head to the acetabulum.
The tibial tuberosity is a bump on the anterior tibia, below the knee, where the patellar ligament attaches. It is on a different bone and the opposite surface.

The intercondylar fossa is also on the posterior femur, but it is the notch between the two condyles at the distal end, not a ridge down the shaft. Pick it if the question asked about the notch between the femoral condyles.
Correct. The linea aspera is the rough ridge down the posterior femoral shaft.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: What is the large opening in the hip bone framed by the ischium and the pubis called?
questions.why: The obturator foramen is the largest opening in the skeleton, a big hole in the lower hip bone surrounded by the ischium and the pubis. It sits just below and in front of the acetabulum. In life it is mostly closed over by a membrane, with a small gap for vessels and a nerve to reach the thigh.
notes: Correct. The obturator foramen is the large opening framed by the ischium and pubis.

The greater sciatic notch is a deep notch on the posterior border of the ilium, not a full ring framed by the ischium and pubis. Pick it if the question asked where the sciatic nerve leaves the pelvis.
The acetabulum is the socket where all three hip bones meet, and it holds the head of the femur. It is a cup, not an opening, so it would be the answer for the hip socket.
The pubic symphysis is the cartilage joint where the two pubic bones meet at the front midline. It would fit a question about where the left and right hip bones join anteriorly.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: The auricular surface of the ilium joins which bone at the sacroiliac joint?
questions.why: The auricular surface is the ear-shaped area on the posterior, medial side of the ilium. It meets a matching auricular surface on the side of the sacrum, forming the sacroiliac joint. This joint is where the weight of the upper body passes from the vertebral column into the pelvic girdle and on to the legs.
notes: The coccyx is the tailbone at the bottom of the sacrum. It does not touch the ilium, so it would only be the answer if the question asked which bone articulates with the inferior tip of the sacrum.
The fifth lumbar vertebra sits on top of the sacrum at the lumbosacral joint. Pick it if the question asked which vertebra rests directly on the sacrum.
The pubis is part of the same hip bone, at the front. It meets the opposite pubis at the pubic symphysis, so it would be the answer for that anterior joint.
Correct. The auricular surface of the ilium articulates with the sacrum at the sacroiliac joint.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which leg bone is the weight-bearing bone, and on which side of the leg does it lie?
options: The tibia, on the medial side
The tibia, on the lateral side
The fibula, on the lateral side
The fibula, on the medial side
questions.why: The tibia is the thick shin bone on the medial side of the leg, and it carries the body's weight from the femur down to the talus. The fibula lies lateral to it and is slender because it does not bear body weight. Remembering that the tibia is medial also tells you that the medial malleolus at the ankle belongs to the tibia.
notes: Correct. The tibia is the weight-bearing bone, and it lies on the medial side of the leg.
The tibia is the weight-bearing bone, but it lies medially, not laterally. Students who picture the leg from behind or flip their own leg in their head often swap the sides.
The fibula is on the lateral side, but it does not bear body weight. It would be the answer if the question asked which leg bone is slender and lateral.
The fibula is neither weight-bearing nor medial. This choice reverses both facts, so it reflects mixing up which leg bone is which.
questions.answerText: The tibia, on the medial side

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: The medial malleolus is the bump on the inner side of the ankle. Which bone bears it?
questions.why: The medial malleolus is the distal end of the tibia, which projects downward on the medial side of the ankle. Because the tibia is the medial bone of the leg, its malleolus is the medial one. Together with the lateral malleolus of the fibula, it forms the sides of the socket that holds the talus at the ankle joint.
notes: The calcaneus is the heel bone, below and behind the ankle joint. It would be the answer if the question asked which bone forms the heel.
The fibula bears the lateral malleolus, the bump on the outer side of the ankle. Pick it if the question asked about the outer ankle bump.
The talus sits between the two malleoli and fits into the socket they form. It has no malleolus of its own, so it would be the answer for the tarsal bone that articulates with both leg bones.
Correct. The medial malleolus is part of the tibia.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which bone bears the lateral malleolus at the ankle?
questions.why: The lateral malleolus is the distal end of the fibula, the bump on the outer side of the ankle. The fibula is the lateral bone of the leg, so its malleolus is the lateral one. It sits a little lower than the medial malleolus and is the common site of an ankle fracture after a rolled ankle.
notes: The talus sits between the two malleoli and carries no malleolus itself. Pick it if the question asked which tarsal fits between the tibia and fibula.
The tibia bears the medial malleolus on the inner side of the ankle. It would be the answer if the question asked about the medial bump.
The femur is the thigh bone and ends at the knee, far above the ankle. Its distal markings are the condyles and epicondyles, so it would fit a question about the knee end of the thigh.
Correct. The lateral malleolus belongs to the fibula.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which tarsal bone articulates with the tibia and fibula and receives the body's weight from the leg?
questions.why: The talus is the highest tarsal bone. It fits between the medial and lateral malleoli and articulates with the tibia above, forming the ankle (talocrural) joint. Weight passes from the tibia to the talus, and from there it spreads back to the calcaneus and forward through the other tarsals to the metatarsals.
notes: The calcaneus is the heel bone below the talus. It receives weight from the talus, not directly from the leg, so it would be the answer for the largest tarsal or the heel bone.
The navicular lies in front of the talus on the medial side of the foot. Pick it if the question asked which tarsal sits between the talus and the cuneiforms.
Correct. The talus articulates with the tibia and fibula and takes the body's weight from the leg.
The cuboid lies on the lateral side of the foot, in front of the calcaneus. It would be the answer for the lateral tarsal that meets the fourth and fifth metatarsals.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: The tibial tuberosity on the front of the tibia is the attachment site for which structure?
questions.why: The tibial tuberosity is the roughened bump on the anterior tibia just below the knee. The patellar ligament runs from the patella down to this tuberosity. Because the patellar ligament is really the continuation of the quadriceps tendon, this bump is where the pull of the quadriceps finally reaches the tibia to extend the knee.
notes: The calcaneal tendon, or Achilles tendon, attaches to the calcaneus at the heel. Choose it if the question asked which tendon anchors to the back of the heel bone.

The quadriceps tendon attaches to the patella, above the knee. It continues below the patella as the patellar ligament, so pick the quadriceps tendon if the question asked what attaches to the base of the patella.
Correct. The patellar ligament anchors on the tibial tuberosity.

The anterior cruciate ligament lies inside the knee joint and attaches to the top of the tibia between the condyles, not to the front of the shaft. It would be the answer for the ligament that stops the tibia sliding forward.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which markings of the femur articulate with the tibia at the knee?
questions.why: The medial and lateral condyles are the large, rounded knobs at the distal femur. Their smooth surfaces rest on the medial and lateral condyles of the tibia, forming the two tibiofemoral joints of the knee. The epicondyles sit just above them and serve as attachment points rather than joint surfaces.
notes: The trochanters are muscle attachment sites at the proximal femur, near the hip. They would be the answer if the question asked for the large projections near the top of the femur.

The epicondyles are the projections just above the condyles where ligaments and muscles attach. They do not touch the tibia, so pick them if the question asked what sits just superior to the condyles.
The head and neck are at the proximal end of the femur. The head articulates with the acetabulum at the hip, so this pair fits a question about the hip joint, not the knee.
Correct. The femoral condyles articulate with the tibia.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: The pubic symphysis is the joint where which structures meet at the front of the pelvis?
questions.why: The pubic symphysis is the midline joint at the front of the pelvis where the left and right pubic bones meet. A disc of fibrocartilage joins them, making it a cartilaginous joint that is slightly movable. It closes the pelvic ring in front, while the sacroiliac joints close it in back.
notes: The ischium and ilium are parts of the same hip bone that fuse at the acetabulum, not at a joint at the front. Pick them only if the question asked which bones fuse together with the pubis to form the hip bone.
The pubis and sacrum are at opposite ends of the pelvis and do not articulate. The sacrum joins the ilium, so the sacroiliac joint is the right answer for where the sacrum meets the hip bone.
The two ilia never meet each other. Each ilium joins the sacrum at a sacroiliac joint in the back, so the ilia would only fit a question about the sacroiliac joints.
Correct. The two pubic bones meet at the pubic symphysis.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: How many phalanges does each toe other than the great toe have?
questions.why: Toes 2 through 5 each have three phalanges: a proximal, a middle, and a distal phalanx. The great toe, the hallux, is the exception, with only a proximal and a distal phalanx. This is the same pattern as the fingers and the thumb.
notes: Two is the number of phalanges in the great toe, the hallux. Pick it if the question asked about the great toe specifically.
One phalanx is too few for any toe. This answer usually comes from thinking of each toe as a single bone, when even the hallux has two.
Four phalanges do not occur in any normal human toe. Students choosing four may be adding the metatarsal to the toe's three phalanges.
Correct. Each of the four lateral toes has three phalanges.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which bones, together with the sacrum and coccyx, form the bony pelvis?
questions.why: The bony pelvis is a ring made of the two hip bones in front and on the sides, closed in back by the sacrum and coccyx. Each hip bone includes the fused ilium, ischium, and pubis, so it takes the whole hip bone, not just the ilium, to complete the ring. The femurs attach to the pelvis but are not part of it.
notes: Correct. The two hip bones plus the sacrum and coccyx form the bony pelvis.

The ilia are only the upper parts of the hip bones. Leaving out the ischium and pubis would leave the front and bottom of the pelvic ring open. This choice would fit a question about which part of each hip bone joins the sacrum.
The lumbar vertebrae sit above the sacrum in the lower back. They carry weight down to the pelvis but are not part of it. They would fit a question about the vertebral region just above the sacrum.
The femurs are the thigh bones. They articulate with the pelvis at the acetabula but belong to the free lower limb. Pick them if the question asked which bones form the hip joints with the pelvis.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: The strong, roughened knob of the ischium that you sit on is which marking?
questions.why: The ischial tuberosity is the thick, rough knob at the bottom of the ischium. When you sit upright, your weight rests on the left and right ischial tuberosities, which is why they are often called the sitting bones. Their rough surface also anchors the hamstring muscles.
notes: The iliac crest is the curved upper rim of the ilium where you rest your hands. It would fit a question about the top border of the hip bone.

The ischial spine is a pointed projection on the ischium just above the tuberosity. It points into the pelvis rather than down toward a seat, so pick it if the question asked for the pointed projection above the sitting knob.
Correct. The ischial tuberosity is the knob you sit on.
The pubic crest is the ridge on the upper border of the pubis, at the front of the pelvis. It would be the answer for the ridge near the front midline.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: The fovea capitis is a small pit found on which part of the femur?
questions.why: The fovea capitis is a small pit near the center of the femoral head. A ligament runs from this pit to the acetabulum, helping anchor the head in the socket, and a small artery travels with it. Its name means pit of the head, which is a quick way to remember where it is.
notes: The neck is the narrow region just below the head. It has no pit, and it would be the answer if the question asked for the common site of a hip fracture.
The lateral condyle is at the distal femur, at the knee. It would be the answer if the question asked which knob of the femur rests on the lateral tibial condyle.
Correct. The fovea capitis sits on the femoral head.
The greater trochanter is the large lateral bump at the proximal femur where hip muscles attach. Pick it if the question asked about the large lateral projection.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: What is the broad superior border of the patella called?
questions.why: The patella is shaped like a rounded triangle pointing down. Its broad top edge is called the base, and its pointed bottom tip is called the apex. The quadriceps tendon attaches along the base, and the patellar ligament leaves from the apex.
notes: The apex is the pointed inferior tip of the patella, the opposite end from the base. Pick it if the question asked about the lower point where the patellar ligament begins.
Correct. The broad superior border of the patella is its base.
A crest is a ridge, as in the iliac crest or pubic crest, and the patella has no marking by that name. This choice comes from borrowing a name used for ridges on other bones.
A fovea is a small pit, as in the fovea capitis of the femoral head. The patella has no fovea, so this choice reflects mixing up markings from different bones.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: How many metatarsals form the sole of the foot, and how are they numbered?
options: Five, numbered I to V starting at the great toe
Fourteen, numbered so each matches a phalanx
Seven, numbered I to VII starting at the great toe
Five, numbered I to V starting at the little toe
questions.why: Each foot has five metatarsals, one behind each toe. They are numbered I to V from medial to lateral, so metatarsal I sits behind the great toe (the hallux) and metatarsal V sits behind the little toe. The same medial-to-lateral numbering is used for the toes themselves.
notes: Correct. There are five metatarsals, numbered I to V from the great toe side.
Fourteen is the number of phalanges in one foot. That count would be right if the question asked about the toe bones, not the metatarsals.
Seven is the number of tarsal bones, not metatarsals. Pick seven if the question asked how many tarsals form the ankle and back of the foot.
The count is right, but the numbering runs from the medial side, so metatarsal I is behind the great toe, not the little toe. Students reverse it when they forget that digit I is the hallux.
questions.answerText: Five, numbered I to V starting at the great toe

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which three arches spread body weight across the foot?
options: The anterior and posterior longitudinal arches and the transverse arch
The medial and lateral transverse arches and the longitudinal arch
The medial and lateral longitudinal arches and the transverse arch
The medial, intermediate, and lateral longitudinal arches
questions.why: The foot has two longitudinal arches running front to back, a higher medial one and a lower lateral one, plus one transverse arch running side to side across the foot. Together they spread weight between the heel and the balls of the foot and spring back with each step. When the medial longitudinal arch drops, the result is flat feet.
notes: Longitudinal arches run front to back, so they are named for the side of the foot they are on, medial and lateral, not anterior and posterior. This choice mixes up direction terms.
This flips the two arch types. There is only one transverse arch, running across the foot, and two longitudinal arches, one medial and one lateral.
Correct. The foot has medial and lateral longitudinal arches and a transverse arch.
There is no intermediate longitudinal arch. This choice borrows the medial, intermediate, and lateral naming used for the three cuneiform bones.
questions.answerText: The medial and lateral longitudinal arches and the transverse arch

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: A clinician feels for the prominent bony point at the front end of the iliac crest to locate an injection site. Which marking is it?
questions.why: The anterior superior iliac spine, often shortened to ASIS, is the point where the iliac crest ends at the front. It sits just under the skin, so clinicians can feel it to find injection sites and check whether the pelvis is level. The anterior inferior iliac spine lies a little below it and is much harder to feel.
notes: The ischial spine is a pointed projection on the ischium inside the pelvis, not on the iliac crest. It would be the answer for the projection just above the ischial tuberosity.
Correct. The anterior superior iliac spine is the palpable point at the front of the iliac crest.

The anterior inferior iliac spine is on the front of the ilium, but it sits below the ASIS and is not the end of the crest. Choose it if the question asked for the projection just below the anterior superior iliac spine.

The posterior superior iliac spine is at the back end of the iliac crest, near the sacroiliac joint. Pick it if the question asked for the point at the back of the crest, often seen as a dimple in the lower back.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Moving distally from the knee along the medial side of the leg, which bone do you follow down to the ankle?
questions.why: The tibia is the medial bone of the leg, so tracing the inner side of the leg from knee to ankle follows the tibia the whole way. It begins with its medial and lateral condyles at the knee and ends in the medial malleolus, the inner ankle bump. Its sharp anterior border is the shin you can feel under the skin.
notes: The femur is the thigh bone and ends at the knee. It would be the answer if the path ran from the hip to the knee instead.
The talus is a tarsal bone at the ankle where the path ends, not the bone you follow down the leg. Choose it if the question asked which bone the tibia rests on at the ankle.
The fibula runs along the lateral side of the leg, from its head just below the knee to the lateral malleolus. Pick it if the question traced the outer side of the leg.
Correct. The tibia runs along the medial side of the leg from knee to ankle.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which marking is the rounded ball at the proximal end of the femur that seats into the hip socket?
questions.why: The head of the femur is the smooth, rounded ball at the top of the bone. It fits into the acetabulum of the hip bone to form the hip joint, a ball-and-socket joint. The narrower neck connects the head to the shaft, and the small pit on the head is the fovea capitis.
notes: The neck is the narrow region just below the head that angles toward the shaft. It would be the answer if the question asked about the common hip fracture site.
The lateral condyle is a rounded knob at the distal femur that rests on the tibia at the knee. It would be the answer for a knee joint surface, not the hip.
Correct. The head of the femur is the ball that seats into the acetabulum.
The greater trochanter is a large lateral bump near the top of the femur where hip muscles attach. It does not enter the socket, so pick it if the question asked for the big lateral projection.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which marking is the deep notch on the posterior border of the ilium?
questions.why: The greater sciatic notch is a large, deep notch on the posterior border of the ilium, above the ischial spine. The sciatic nerve, the largest nerve in the body, passes through it from the pelvis into the gluteal region. A smaller notch, the lesser sciatic notch, lies below the ischial spine on the ischium.
notes: The auricular surface is the ear-shaped joint surface on the medial ilium that meets the sacrum. It would be the answer for the part of the ilium that forms the sacroiliac joint.
The lesser sciatic notch is the smaller notch below the ischial spine, on the ischium rather than the ilium. Pick it if the question asked for the notch just under the ischial spine.
Correct. The greater sciatic notch is the deep notch on the posterior border of the ilium.
The obturator foramen is a full opening in the lower hip bone framed by the ischium and pubis, not a notch on the posterior border. It would be the answer for the largest hole in the hip bone.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which tarsal bone sits directly under the talus and forms the back of the foot?
questions.why: The calcaneus lies directly beneath the talus and projects backward to form the heel. It is the largest tarsal and takes the impact of heel strike. The talus passes weight down to it, and from there the load spreads forward through the other tarsals to the metatarsals.
notes: The cuboid lies in front of the calcaneus on the lateral side of the foot. It would be the answer for the lateral tarsal that meets metatarsals IV and V.
The medial cuneiform is one of three wedge-shaped tarsals in the front row, in line with the great toe. Choose it if the question asked which tarsal articulates with metatarsal I.
Correct. The calcaneus sits under the talus and forms the heel.
The navicular lies in front of the talus on the medial side of the foot, not underneath it. Pick it if the question asked for the tarsal between the talus and the cuneiforms.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which marking is the pointed projection of the ischium located just above the ischial tuberosity?
questions.why: The ischial spine is a pointed projection on the posterior ischium that sits above the ischial tuberosity and points toward the inside of the pelvis. It separates the greater sciatic notch above it from the lesser sciatic notch below it. It also serves as an attachment point for a ligament that runs to the sacrum.
notes: The pubic crest is the ridge on the upper border of the pubis at the front of the pelvis. It would be the answer for the ridge near the pubic symphysis.
The iliac crest is the curved upper rim of the ilium where you rest your hands. It would fit a question about the top border of the hip bone.
Correct. The ischial spine is the pointed projection just above the tuberosity.
The ischial tuberosity is the rough knob below the spine that you sit on. Pick it if the question asked which part of the ischium bears weight when sitting.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which femoral marking is the notch between the distal condyles on the posterior surface?
questions.why: The intercondylar fossa is the deep notch between the medial and lateral condyles on the back of the distal femur. The cruciate ligaments of the knee attach inside this notch. On the front of the distal femur, the condyles are joined instead by the smooth patellar surface where the kneecap glides.
notes: The linea aspera is also on the posterior femur, but it is a ridge running down the shaft, above the condyles. Pick it if the question asked about the rough line on the back of the shaft.
Correct. The intercondylar fossa is the notch between the femoral condyles on the posterior side.
The greater trochanter is a large lateral projection at the proximal femur. It would fit a question about the big bump on the side of the hip.
The fovea capitis is a small pit on the femoral head at the hip end. It would be the answer for the pit where a ligament anchors the head to the acetabulum.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: The sharp anterior border felt directly under the skin as the shin belongs to which bone?
questions.why: The tibia has a sharp anterior border, also called the anterior crest, that runs down the front of the leg just under the skin. That ridge is what you feel as your shin. Because there is so little soft tissue over it, a blow to the shin hurts and a fracture there is easy to feel.
notes: Correct. The anterior border of the tibia forms the shin.
The femur is the thigh bone, above the knee. Its shaft is wrapped in thick muscle and cannot be felt as a sharp edge, so it would fit a question about the bone of the thigh.
The patella is the kneecap at the front of the knee, not along the shin. Choose it if the question asked which bone you feel at the front of the knee.

The fibula is on the lateral side of the leg and is covered by muscle along most of its length. Only its head and lateral malleolus are easy to feel, so pick it if the question asked about the outer ankle bump.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Following the lateral side of the leg from knee to ankle, which proximal marking and which bone are you tracking?
options: The head of the fibula and the fibula
The lateral condyle and the tibia
The greater trochanter and the femur
The medial malleolus and the tibia
questions.why: The fibula is the slender lateral bone of the leg. Its proximal end is a knob called the head, which you can feel on the outer side of the leg just below the knee, and its distal end is the lateral malleolus. Following the outer leg from knee to ankle traces this bone from head to malleolus.
notes: Correct. The lateral leg is the fibula, which starts proximally at its head.

The tibia does have a lateral condyle, but the tibia is the medial bone of the leg, so following it would trace the inner side. Pick this pair if the question asked which tibial marking the fibular head sits under.
The greater trochanter and femur are at the hip and thigh, above the knee. This pair would fit a path along the lateral thigh, not the leg.
The medial malleolus is the distal end of the tibia on the inner ankle, the opposite side and opposite end from this path. It would be the answer for the inner ankle bump.
questions.answerText: The head of the fibula and the fibula

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which region is the narrower ring of the pelvis below the pelvic brim?
questions.why: The pelvic brim is a rim of bone that divides the pelvis into two regions. Below it is the true pelvis, a narrower ring that surrounds the pelvic cavity and forms the birth canal. Above it is the false pelvis, the wide flare of the ilia that supports the lower abdominal organs.
notes: The iliac fossa is the concave inner surface of the ilium, which forms the wall of the false pelvis. It would fit a question about the smooth inner face of the ilium.
The false pelvis is the wide flare above the pelvic brim, formed mainly by the ilia. Pick it if the question asked for the region above the brim.
The pelvic brim is the dividing line itself, not a region. It would be the answer if the question asked what separates the true and false pelvis.
Correct. The true pelvis is the narrower ring below the pelvic brim.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which femoral marking is the smaller projection on the medial side near the proximal end?
questions.why: The lesser trochanter is a small, rounded projection on the medial and slightly posterior side of the proximal femur, just below the neck. It is a muscle attachment site. The much larger greater trochanter sits on the lateral side at about the same level.
notes: The medial epicondyle is a medial projection at the distal end, just above the medial condyle. It would fit a question about the attachment bump above the knee joint surface.
The greater trochanter is the large projection on the lateral side of the proximal femur. Pick it if the question asked for the big lateral bump.
Correct. The lesser trochanter is the small medial projection at the proximal femur.
The medial condyle is on the medial side, but at the distal end of the femur, where it rests on the tibia. It would be the answer for a knee joint surface.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which marking is the pointed inferior tip of the kneecap?
questions.why: The patella is roughly triangular, with its point facing down. That pointed inferior tip is the apex, and the broad superior border is the base. The patellar ligament leaves the apex and runs down to the tibial tuberosity.
notes: The base is the broad superior border of the patella, the opposite end from the apex. Pick it if the question asked about the top edge where the quadriceps tendon attaches.
Correct. The apex is the pointed inferior tip of the patella.
The tibial tuberosity is a bump on the anterior tibia below the knee where the patellar ligament ends. Choose it if the question asked where the patellar ligament attaches.
The lateral condyle is a knob of the femur or tibia that forms part of the knee joint surface, not a part of the patella. It would be the answer for a joint surface at the knee.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Tracing the bones of the free lower limb from the hip, which bone comes first, and which two follow it in the leg?
options: The tibia first, then the femur and the fibula
The patella first, then the femur and the tibia
The femur first, then the tibia and the fibula
The fibula first, then the tibia and the femur
questions.why: The free lower limb begins with the thigh, which has a single bone, the femur, running from the hip to the knee. Below the knee is the leg, which has two parallel bones, the medial tibia and the lateral fibula. The pattern of one bone and then two matches the upper limb, with the humerus followed by the radius and ulna.
notes: The tibia is in the leg, below the knee, so it cannot come before the femur. This order puts a leg bone in the thigh.
The patella sits in front of the knee, between the femur and tibia, not at the hip. Pick the patella if the question asked which bone lies in front of the knee joint.
Correct. The femur comes first, then the tibia and fibula in the leg.
The fibula is a leg bone that does not even reach the knee joint, so it cannot be first. This order reflects starting at the wrong end of the limb.
questions.answerText: The femur first, then the tibia and the fibula

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Trace the bones of the free lower limb in order from the hip joint to the tip of a toe, not counting the hip bone.
options: Femur, tibia and fibula, metatarsal, tarsals, phalanges
Femur, tibia and fibula, tarsals, metatarsal, phalanges
Hip bone, femur, tibia, metatarsal, phalanges
Femur, tarsals, tibia and fibula, metatarsal, phalanges
questions.why: Starting at the hip, the femur spans the thigh to the knee. The tibia and fibula span the leg to the ankle, where the tarsals form the ankle and back of the foot. A metatarsal then runs through the sole to the base of a toe, and the phalanges form the toe itself.
notes: This swaps the tarsals and the metatarsal. The tarsals form the ankle and back of the foot, and the metatarsals lie in front of them, so tarsals come first.
Correct. Femur, tibia and fibula, tarsals, metatarsal, phalanges.

This sequence starts with the hip bone, which the question excludes because it belongs to the pelvic girdle, and it also skips the fibula and the tarsals. It would only fit a question that asked to include the girdle.
This puts the tarsals in the thigh region, before the leg bones. The tarsals form the ankle, so they come after the tibia and fibula, not before.
questions.answerText: Femur, tibia and fibula, tarsals, metatarsal, phalanges

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which set correctly names a pelvic girdle bone, the thigh bone, and the socket where they articulate?
options: The hip bone, the femur, and the obturator foramen
The hip bone, the tibia, and the acetabulum
The sacrum, the femur, and the acetabulum
The hip bone, the femur, and the acetabulum
questions.why: The pelvic girdle is made of the two hip bones, and each one meets the thigh bone, the femur, at the hip joint. The socket of that joint is the acetabulum, a deep cup on the lateral hip bone that receives the head of the femur. This ball-and-socket arrangement links the lower limb to the axial skeleton.
notes: The obturator foramen is a large opening in the hip bone below the acetabulum, not a socket. Nothing articulates in it, so it would only be the answer for the opening framed by the ischium and pubis.
The tibia is a leg bone that articulates with the femur at the knee, not with the hip bone. This set would fit only if the question asked about the knee.
The sacrum is an axial bone, not part of the pelvic girdle, and it never meets the femur. It joins the hip bone at the sacroiliac joint, so pick the sacrum for that joint.
Correct. The hip bone and femur articulate at the acetabulum.
questions.answerText: The hip bone, the femur, and the acetabulum

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which statement correctly matches each leg bone to the malleolus at its ankle end?
options: The fibula carries both malleoli and the tibia carries neither
The tibia carries the lateral malleolus and the fibula carries the medial malleolus
The tibia carries both malleoli and the fibula carries neither
The tibia carries the medial malleolus and the fibula carries the lateral malleolus
questions.why: Each leg bone ends in one malleolus, and the name follows the side the bone is on. The tibia is the medial leg bone, so its distal end is the medial malleolus, the inner ankle bump. The fibula is lateral, so its distal end is the lateral malleolus, the outer ankle bump.
notes: The fibula carries only the lateral malleolus. Giving it both bumps comes from thinking of the fibula as the ankle bone and the tibia as the knee bone.
This reverses the pairing. The tibia is the medial bone, so it cannot carry the lateral malleolus. Students who mix up which leg bone is medial fall into this swap.
The tibia carries only the medial malleolus. The outer ankle bump belongs to the fibula, so this choice ignores the fibula's distal end.
Correct. Tibia with the medial malleolus, fibula with the lateral malleolus.
questions.answerText: The tibia carries the medial malleolus and the fibula carries the lateral malleolus

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Name the three regions of the hip bone in this order: the superior fan-shaped part, the posteroinferior part, and the anteromedial part.
questions.why: The ilium is the broad, fan-shaped upper part of the hip bone, topped by the iliac crest. The ischium forms the posterior and lower part, including the ischial tuberosity you sit on. The pubis forms the front, medial part and meets the other pubis at the pubic symphysis.
notes: Correct. Ilium is superior, ischium is posteroinferior, and pubis is anteromedial.
The ischium is posteroinferior, not the fan-shaped top. The fan-shaped superior part is the ilium, which holds the iliac crest.
This reverses the order. The pubis is the anteromedial part, not the superior fan, so it belongs last in this sequence.
The ilium is right, but the pubis is anteromedial and the ischium is posteroinferior. This choice swaps the last two.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Comparing the two ends of the leg bones, which statement correctly describes where the knee condyles and the malleoli are found?
options: The fibula bears the condyles and the medial malleolus, and the tibia bears the head and the lateral malleolus
The tibia bears the condyles and the lateral malleolus, and the fibula bears the head and the medial malleolus
The tibia bears the condyles and the medial malleolus, and the fibula bears the head and the lateral malleolus
The tibia bears the head and the medial malleolus, and the fibula bears the condyles and the lateral malleolus
questions.why: Only the tibia forms part of the knee joint, so only the tibia has condyles that meet the femur. Its distal end is the medial malleolus. The fibula is a slender lateral bone that stays out of the knee joint, with a simple head at its proximal end and the lateral malleolus at its distal end.
notes: This swaps the bones completely. The fibula never touches the femur, so it has no knee condyles, and it is lateral, so it carries the lateral malleolus.
The proximal ends are right, but the malleoli are reversed. The tibia is medial, so it ends in the medial malleolus.
Correct. The tibia has the condyles and medial malleolus, and the fibula has the head and lateral malleolus.
The malleoli are right, but the proximal ends are swapped. The tibia is the bone with condyles at the knee, and the fibula ends proximally in its head.
questions.answerText: The tibia bears the condyles and the medial malleolus, and the fibula bears the head and the lateral malleolus

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Trace the path of body weight from the sacrum to the femur, naming the bones and joints in order.
options: Sacrum to ilium at the sacroiliac joint, then acetabulum to femoral head at the hip joint
Sacrum to pubis at the pubic symphysis, then acetabulum to femoral head at the hip joint
Sacrum to ischium at the acetabulum, then ilium to femoral neck at the hip joint
Sacrum to ilium at the sacroiliac joint, then obturator foramen to femoral head at the hip joint
questions.why: Weight from the vertebral column reaches the sacrum and passes sideways into each ilium through the sacroiliac joint, where the auricular surfaces of the two bones meet. The hip bone then carries the load down to the acetabulum. The acetabulum receives the head of the femur at the hip joint, passing the weight into the thigh.
notes: Correct. Sacrum to ilium at the sacroiliac joint, then acetabulum to femoral head at the hip.
The sacrum does not touch the pubis. The pubic symphysis joins the two pubic bones at the front, so this path would only fit a question about the front of the pelvic ring.
The sacrum meets the ilium, not the ischium, and the femur articulates by its head, not its neck. This choice mixes up both the joint partners and the femoral marking.
The first joint is right, but the obturator foramen is an opening, not a socket, and the femur does not articulate there. The femoral head sits in the acetabulum.
questions.answerText: Sacrum to ilium at the sacroiliac joint, then acetabulum to femoral head at the hip joint

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: How many bones fuse to form each hip bone?
questions.why: Each hip bone forms from three bones, the ilium, the ischium, and the pubis, which are separate in a child and fuse at the acetabulum by early adulthood. That is why the adult hip bone has three named regions even though it is one bone. Two hip bones, along with the sacrum and coccyx, make up the bony pelvis.
notes: Four would come from adding the sacrum to the hip bone. The sacrum joins the hip bone at the sacroiliac joint but is a separate axial bone.
Correct. The ilium, ischium, and pubis fuse to form each hip bone.
Two leaves out one of the three regions. Students sometimes forget the ischium or count only the large ilium and the pubis at the front.
Five is the number of vertebrae that fuse to form the sacrum. Pick it if the question asked how many vertebrae fuse into the sacrum.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which part of the hip bone is the large, fan-shaped superior portion?
questions.why: The ilium is the largest part of the hip bone, a broad, flared blade that forms its upper portion. Its upper rim is the iliac crest, its smooth inner surface is the iliac fossa, and its auricular surface joins the sacrum. The ilium also forms the upper part of the acetabulum.
notes: Correct. The ilium is the large fan-shaped upper part of the hip bone.
The acetabulum is the deep socket on the side of the hip bone where all three parts meet. It is a cup, not a fan-shaped blade, so it would fit a question about the hip socket.
The pubis is the anteromedial part of the hip bone that meets its partner at the pubic symphysis. It would be the answer for the front, medial region.
The ischium is the posteroinferior part of the hip bone, including the ischial tuberosity you sit on. Pick it if the question asked for the lower back part.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: What is the deep cup where the ilium, ischium, and pubis meet and fuse?
questions.why: The acetabulum is the deep socket on the lateral surface of the hip bone, and each of the three parts, the ilium, ischium, and pubis, contributes a piece of it. Their fusion lines meet in the cup. The acetabulum receives the head of the femur to form the hip joint.
notes: The iliac fossa is the smooth inner surface of the ilium alone. Pick it if the question asked for the concave inner face of the ilium.
The obturator foramen is the large opening framed by the ischium and pubis only, below the acetabulum. It is a hole, not a cup, so it would be the answer for that opening.

The pubic symphysis is where the left and right pubic bones meet at the front midline. It joins two separate hip bones rather than the three parts of one, so it fits a question about the front joint of the pelvis.
Correct. The three hip bone regions meet in the acetabulum.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which bone is the longest and strongest bone in the body?
questions.why: The femur, the thigh bone, is the longest and strongest bone in the body. It carries the full weight of the upper body from the hip to the knee and anchors the large muscles of the thigh and hip. Its length also makes up a big share of a person's standing height.
notes: The fibula is long but slender and does not bear body weight. It would fit a question about the thin lateral bone of the leg.
The humerus is the longest bone of the upper limb, but it does not carry body weight and is shorter than the femur. Pick it if the question asked about the arm.
The tibia is the second longest bone and the main weight-bearing bone of the leg, but it is shorter than the femur. It would be the answer for the strongest bone below the knee.
Correct. The femur is the longest and strongest bone in the body.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: In the classification of bones by shape, the kneecap is which type?
questions.why: The patella is a sesamoid bone, meaning a bone that forms within a tendon. It develops inside the quadriceps tendon at the front of the knee. Sesamoid bones protect the tendon and improve its leverage as it slides over the joint.
notes: Correct. The patella is a sesamoid bone that forms in the quadriceps tendon.
An irregular bone has a complex shape that fits no other category, such as a vertebra. Choose it if the question asked how a vertebra is classified.
A flat bone is thin and plate-like, such as the sternum or the bones of the skull roof. It would be the answer for a bone like the parietal.
A long bone is longer than it is wide, with a shaft and two ends, like the femur or tibia. Pick it if the question asked how the femur is classified.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: What is the small pit on the head of the femur called?
questions.why: The fovea capitis is a small pit near the center of the femoral head. It anchors a ligament that runs to the acetabulum, helping hold the head in its socket, and a small artery to the head travels in that ligament. The name means pit of the head.
notes: The linea aspera is the rough ridge down the back of the femoral shaft, a muscle attachment line. Pick it if the question asked about the ridge on the posterior shaft.
Correct. The fovea capitis is the pit on the femoral head.
The greater trochanter is a large lateral projection, the opposite of a pit. Choose it if the question asked for the big bump on the side of the proximal femur.
The intercondylar fossa is a notch, but it lies between the condyles at the distal femur, not on the head. It would be the answer for the notch at the back of the knee end of the femur.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which bony bump of the ankle belongs to the tibia?
questions.why: The distal end of the tibia projects downward on the inner side of the ankle as the medial malleolus. The tibia is the medial leg bone, so its ankle bump is the medial one. The two malleoli together form the sides of the socket that holds the talus.
notes: The tibial tuberosity is on the tibia, but at the front of the bone just below the knee, where the patellar ligament attaches. It would be the answer for the bump below the kneecap.
The head of the fibula is the knob at the top of the fibula, below the lateral knee. It belongs to the other leg bone and the other end of the leg.
The lateral malleolus is the outer ankle bump, and it belongs to the fibula. Pick it if the question asked which ankle bump belongs to the fibula.
Correct. The medial malleolus is the tibia's ankle bump.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: A surgeon removes a length of one leg bone to use as a bone graft because that bone does not carry body weight. Which bone is it?
questions.why: The fibula is the slender lateral bone of the leg, and it does not carry the body's weight. Its main jobs are anchoring muscles and forming the lateral side of the ankle. Because the tibia carries the load, a segment of the fibula's shaft can be removed for a graft while the person can still stand and walk.
notes: Correct. The fibula does not bear body weight, so part of it can be harvested as a graft.
The patella is a small sesamoid bone in the quadriceps tendon, not a long bone with a shaft to harvest. It would fit a question about the bone in front of the knee.
The tibia is the weight-bearing bone of the leg, so removing part of it would leave the leg unable to support the body. It would be the answer if the question asked which leg bone carries the weight.
The femur carries the entire weight of the body through the thigh. Pick it if the question asked for the longest and strongest bone.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Which surface of the hip bone joins the sacrum at the sacroiliac joint?
questions.why: The auricular surface is an ear-shaped area on the medial, posterior part of the ilium. It fits against a matching auricular surface on the side of the sacrum to form the sacroiliac joint. Auricular means ear-shaped, which describes its outline.
notes: The acetabulum is the socket on the lateral hip bone that receives the femoral head. Pick it if the question asked which surface forms the hip joint.
The iliac fossa is the smooth, concave inner surface of the ilium, in front of the auricular surface. It faces the abdomen and does not articulate with any bone.
Correct. The auricular surface of the ilium meets the sacrum.
The pubic symphysis is the joint where the two pubic bones meet at the front of the pelvis. It would be the answer if the question asked where the hip bones join each other anteriorly.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Besides the talus and the calcaneus, which bones make up the other five tarsals?
options: The navicular, the cuboid, and three metatarsals
The scaphoid, the cuboid, and the three cuneiforms
The navicular, the cuboid, and the three cuneiforms
The navicular, the hamate, and the three cuneiforms
questions.why: The seven tarsals are the talus, the calcaneus, the navicular, the cuboid, and the medial, intermediate, and lateral cuneiforms. The navicular sits in front of the talus on the medial side, the cuboid sits in front of the calcaneus on the lateral side, and the three cuneiforms lie in front of the navicular.
notes: The navicular and cuboid are right, but the metatarsals are the five bones of the sole in front of the tarsals, not tarsals themselves. Pick metatarsals if the question asked about the bones between the tarsals and the toes.

The scaphoid is a carpal bone of the wrist, not a tarsal. Students mix it up with the navicular because both are boat-shaped, and in older books the scaphoid was even called the navicular of the hand.
Correct. The navicular, cuboid, and three cuneiforms complete the seven tarsals.
The hamate is a carpal bone of the wrist with a hook-like process. This choice borrows a wrist bone into the foot, which is a common mix-up between carpals and tarsals.
questions.answerText: The navicular, the cuboid, and the three cuneiforms

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: A pelvis is wide and shallow, with a broad pubic angle and a large outlet. Which sex does it most likely belong to, and why?
options: Female, because a wider outlet is adapted for childbirth
Male, because a wider pelvis supports a heavier frame
Female, because a shallow pelvis protects the organs better
Male, because a broad pubic angle anchors larger muscles
questions.why: The typical female pelvis is wider and shallower, with a broader pubic angle and a larger outlet. These features enlarge the opening that a baby passes through during birth. The typical male pelvis is narrower and deeper, with a narrower pubic angle and heavier markings.
notes: Correct. The wide, shallow shape with a large outlet is a female adaptation for childbirth.
A male pelvis is narrower and deeper, not wider. A heavier build shows up as thicker bone and more prominent markings rather than a wider ring.
The sex is right, but the reason is wrong. A shallower pelvis does not protect organs better; its shape is adapted to widen the birth canal.
A broad pubic angle is a female trait, not a male one. The male pubic angle is narrower, so this choice reverses the comparison.
questions.answerText: Female, because a wider outlet is adapted for childbirth

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: An older adult with thinned bone falls and fractures the narrow, angled part of the femur just below the head. Which region broke?
questions.why: The femoral neck is the narrow, angled region that connects the head of the femur to the shaft. It is the usual site of a broken hip, especially in older adults whose bone has thinned from osteoporosis. Because the blood supply to the femoral head runs close to the neck, a fracture here can threaten the head itself.
notes: The lateral condyle is at the distal femur, at the knee. It would be the answer for an injury to the knee end of the bone.
The greater trochanter is the large lateral bump below the neck. It can be bruised or broken in a fall, but it is a projection, not the narrow region just below the head.
The linea aspera is a ridge along the back of the femoral shaft. Pick it if the question asked about the muscle attachment line on the posterior shaft.
Correct. The femoral neck is the narrow region below the head and the common hip fracture site.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: A person rolls the ankle so the sole turns inward and fractures the bony bump on the outer side of the ankle. Which marking broke?
options: The lateral malleolus of the fibula
The lateral condyle of the tibia
The medial malleolus of the tibia
questions.why: The bump on the outer side of the ankle is the lateral malleolus, the distal end of the fibula. It is the most common ankle fracture site, often from rolling the ankle. Because the fibula does not bear body weight, this fracture is usually less serious than a break of the tibia.
notes: Correct. The outer ankle bump is the lateral malleolus of the fibula.
The lateral condyle of the tibia is at the knee, where the tibia meets the femur. It would fit a question about a fracture of the tibial joint surface at the knee.
The head of the fibula is on the same bone, but at the proximal end, just below the knee. Pick it if the question described an injury on the outer side of the leg near the knee.
The medial malleolus is the inner ankle bump at the distal tibia. It would be the answer if the injury were on the inner side of the ankle.
questions.answerText: The lateral malleolus of the fibula

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: A patient's footprint shows the whole sole touching the floor, with no gap along the inner edge of the foot. Which structure has dropped?
questions.why: A normal footprint has a curved gap along the inner edge because the medial longitudinal arch lifts that part of the sole off the ground. When this arch drops, the inner sole flattens onto the floor, a condition called flat feet. The arches normally spread weight across the foot and spring back with each step.
notes: The transverse arch runs side to side across the foot, under the tarsals and bases of the metatarsals. It would fit a question about the arch that curves across the width of the foot.
Correct. A dropped medial longitudinal arch produces flat feet.

The lateral longitudinal arch runs along the outer edge of the foot and is naturally low, so the outer sole already touches the ground. It would be the answer only if the question described a change along the outer edge.
The calcaneal tendon attaches to the back of the heel and does not form an arch of the sole. Pick it if the question asked which tendon anchors to the calcaneus.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: The rounded head of the femur sits in a deep cup formed by three fused bones. Which joint is described?
options: The knee joint, at the condyles
The hip joint, at the acetabulum
The sacroiliac joint, at the auricular surface
The ankle joint, at the malleoli
questions.why: The acetabulum is the deep cup where the ilium, ischium, and pubis fuse, and it receives the head of the femur. Together they form the hip joint, a ball-and-socket joint. The depth of the socket makes the hip very stable for carrying body weight.
notes: The knee joint is where the femoral condyles rest on the tibial condyles. These are rounded knobs on fairly flat surfaces, not a ball in a deep cup.
Correct. The femoral head in the acetabulum forms the hip joint.
The sacroiliac joint is where the auricular surface of the ilium meets the sacrum. Pick it if the question asked where the hip bone joins the vertebral column.
The ankle joint is where the talus fits between the tibia and fibula, with the malleoli forming its sides. It does not involve the femur.
questions.answerText: The hip joint, at the acetabulum

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: Following the lower limb from the hip to the knee, which single bone spans that region?
questions.why: The region from the hip to the knee is the thigh, and it contains a single long bone, the femur. Below the knee, the leg has two bones, the tibia and fibula. The patella sits at the knee but is not part of the thigh's skeleton.
notes: Correct. The femur is the only bone of the thigh.
The talus is a tarsal bone at the ankle. It would fit a question about the bone that receives weight from the tibia.
The tibia spans the leg, from the knee to the ankle. It would be the answer if the question asked about the medial bone below the knee.
The fibula spans the lateral leg, from just below the knee to the ankle. Pick it if the question asked about the slender lateral leg bone.

questions.topic: Pelvic girdle and lower limb bones
questions.q: The femur is the longest and strongest bone in the body. Which fact about its position best explains why it must be so strong?
options: It shields the pelvic organs from blows to the side of the hip
It carries the body's weight from the hip to the knee during standing and walking
It anchors the small muscles of the foot that push off during walking
It spans from the hip all the way to the ankle
questions.why: The femur is the only bone in the thigh, so all the weight of the head, trunk, and upper limbs passes through it on the way from the pelvis to the knee. Walking, running, and jumping multiply those forces. Large thigh and hip muscles also pull on it, so its thick, strong shaft is built to resist heavy loads.
